description: Frozen seed inventory: 757 curated EVM exploit reports used as discovery leads, complete through July 2026. Row coordinates (source.file, source.incidentIndex) are stable row identities within this inventory.

incident.name: 0VIX vGHST collateral price manipulation
incident.notes: The market worked as designed; 0VIX priced vGHST collateral from the vGHST vault's own GHST-per-share rate, and the attacker inflated that rate by pushing GHST into the vault so a small ovGHST position could borrow out the other 0VIX markets.

sources.ref: onchain review: ovGHST market 0xe053a4014b50666ed388ab8cbb18d5834de0ab12 created 2023-03-17 by 0x8e1304ea39c47e791182ba39fdf362a8767d7e97 (0VIX deployer), unrelated to attack sender 0x702ef63881b5241ffb412199547bcd0c6910a970; a single EIP-1967 Upgraded event fired in the creation block itself, so lastChange = deployment and the code was 42 days old

incident.name: 0x8d2e
incident.notes: uniswapV3SwapCallback lacks access control and transfers all USDC to a caller-specified address.

incident.name: 0xf340
incident.notes: initVRF lacks access control, letting the attacker set a recipient and repeatedly drain LINK via selector 0x607d60e6.

incident.name: 1inch Fusion v1 Settlement calldata corruption (resolver drain)
incident.notes: Yul calldata/memory overflow in Settlement _settleOrder lets a crafted fake interactionLength corrupt the copied calldata and craft a malicious fee suffix.

incident.name: AaveBoost proxyDeposit credits caller with the contract's own balance
incident.notes: AaveBoost.proxyDeposit(token, onBehalfOf, amount) is permissionless and, when called with amount 0, deposits a fixed slice of the helper contract's own AAVE holdings into the Aave pool crediting the caller-supplied beneficiary, so 163 repeated calls transferred the contract's AAVE balance into aAAVE owned by the attacker, who then withdrew it.

sources.ref: onchain review: AaveBoost 0xd2933c86216dC0c938FfAFEca3C8a2D6e633e2cA created 2022-02-15T10:49:38Z by 0xcb7d8a80c3d7d3ebd7fbd0fa6b644c8a536c9269, not the attack-tx sender 0x5d4430d14ae1d11526ddac1c1ef01da3b1dae455; no EIP-1967 events, 1212.6 days old. Reported loss 14.8k USD in AAVE.

incident.name: ParaSwapRepayAdapter V3 unvalidated paraswapData
incident.notes: swapAndRepay/_buyOnParaSwap forwarded caller-supplied paraswapData to Augustus and left the collateral-asset allowance standing, so a crafted swap payload let the attacker pull tokens users had approved to the periphery adapter.

sources.ref: onchain review: adapter 0x02e7b851... created by 0x57dc6c401819ea097db8d4b66d8e35cda0277a73 in tx 0xfebcf4a63b149c5605b46bdfe8a255c7e4435a1990ad535603bd8d75c4a63a0b (2023-07-12), unrelated to attack sender 0x6ea83f23...; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events before the incident

incident.name: Rebalancer arbitrary call abuses delegated Aave credit
incident.notes: The rebalancer executed caller-supplied target/calldata from its own address with no whitelist, so an attacker had it call Aave Pool.borrow(WAVAX, 7000e18, 2, 0, victim) against the WAVAX borrowing power the victim had delegated to it, then transferred the received WAVAX out with a second arbitrary call.

sources.ref: onchain review: rebalancer 0x7A7bAB45363Efb0394Ff27bfA29bb7C0534cA8C9 created 2025-12-31T18:31:23Z by 0x6fdae9edacc6461b21f71a1a6a420197d2b0c3aa (the delegating victim), not the attack-tx sender 0xf59dc5521f191bcb53a9bcbd1654be81b72ee96f; no EIP-1967 events, 108.5 days old. 6,999.91 WAVAX x $9.194 at the incident timestamp (DefiLlama coingecko:avalanche-2) = $64,357.

incident.name: Abracadabra (CauldronV4)
incident.notes: CauldronV4 (yvcrvSTETH): rounding drift in userBorrowPart accounting exploited to zero out borrow shares.

sources.ref: onchain review (no exploit tx in this row; DeFiHackLabs src/test/2024-01/MIMSpell2_exp.sol names the same victim. Incident block located by binary-searching eth_getBlockByNumber to measurement.incidentTimestamp -> ethereum block 19119184, 2024-01-30T12:00:00Z). The victim 0x7259e152103756e1616A77Ae982353c3751A6a90 is an EIP-1167 minimal proxy created at block 16520538, 2023-01-30T15:28:47Z; its 45-byte runtime (0x363d3d373d3d3d363d73c4113ae18e0d3213c6a06947a2ffc70ad3517c775af43d82803e903d91602b57fd5bf3) hardcodes the CauldronV4 master 0xc4113ae18e0d3213c6a06947a2ffc70ad3517c77 in the bytecode rather than in storage, so the delegate target cannot be repointed. The clone runtime is byte-identical at its creation block and the incident block, and the master (created 2023-01-26T02:59:11Z, block 16488159) itself contains zero DELEGATECALL opcodes and emits no EIP-1967 Upgraded event. The effective code therefore never changed after the clone was deployed and the deployment basis is exact.

re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis (re-check of the existing note). The clone's 45-byte runtime and the CauldronV4 master 0xc4113ae18e0d3213c6a06947a2ffc70ad3517c77's 22 kB runtime are each byte-identical at 13 sample points across [16520538, 19119184], so neither the hardcoded delegate target nor the master's code moved before the incident.
exploit tx backfilled and verified onchain (block 19118660): a contract-creation tx deploying and running the exploit, CauldronV4 victim in receipt logs, matching the DeFiHackLabs MIMSpell2 PoC

incident.name: MainPool public calcStepIncome()
incident.notes: MainPool.calcStepIncome(id, amount, step) was callable by anyone with arbitrary arguments and credited the caller's withdrawable income directly, so the attacker joined the game and then wrote itself an income entry it withdrew as ETH.

incident.name: AdsharesBridge
incident.notes: The privileged bridge minter minted wADS to the attacker with fabricated native from/txid values, i.e. the mint authority was used to fake cross-chain deposits.

incident.name: AES deflationary transfer pair-balance flaw
incident.notes: AES's deflationary transfer burns from the liquidity pair's own balance without a sync(), so the attacker shrank the AES reserve and swapped the resulting imbalance out for the pair's USDT.

Loss verified onchain: 61,608.04 USDT left the AES/USDT pair 0x40eD17221b3B2D8455F4F1a05CAc6b77c5f707e3 to the attacker.

incident.name: Pricer ownership manager unrestricted transferOwnership
incident.notes: The pricer-ownership manager deployed with the December oracle upgrade exposed transferOwnership(address,address) with no caller restriction, so the attacker took ownership of the stETH/AAVE/LINK/WBTC pricer proxies, swapped in a malicious pricer implementation, wrote arbitrary expiry prices into the Opyn Oracle and redeemed worthless oTokens against the MarginPool.

sources.ref: callTracer review of the takeover tx: attacker helper 0x1a7efc51... calls 0x9d7b3586... with selector 0x6d435421 (transferOwnership(address,address)), which forwards f2fde38b to pricer proxy 0xa4aC089B972206021EceB50a494d60B1c74E534e, then setImplementation (0xd784d426) to malicious pricer 0xE1f09d50F733993b11bF3054bD870d688401984c and pushes an expiry price into Oracle 0xb5711dAeC960c9487d95bA327c570a7cCE4982c0; the same pattern repeats for 0xb78E96750497e319Bb6a09a8Dc7C75fE32937AdA. Victim creator 0xb594f7e7ad548f63db49665ae4e3d3f8457cf6f5 is not the attacker; the MarginPool drain followed 10 blocks later in tx 0x16eded2553e0793472a6283093738152de1dd0e2504836856fbcaf88cc4a2687 Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the victim's fallback is a non-standard proxy path that DELEGATECALLs whatever address sits in plain storage slot 1 (no EIP-1967 or beacon slot is used); slot 1 reads 0x0 at the incident block 23995254, so that path dead-ends in STOP and every executed instruction comes from the victim's own runtime, which is byte-identical at the creation block 23979057 and the incident block 23995254. The only other DELEGATECALL is an OpenZeppelin Address helper on a target passed in by the caller. Deployment is therefore the right basis, and the flawed transferOwnership(address,address) is code the deployer shipped 2.3 days earlier, not something the attacker installed.

incident.name: Agave
incident.notes: State-changing reentrancy via onTokenTransfer during aToken burn in liquidationCall corrupts accounting.

sources.ref: re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis. The victim is an Aave-fork InitializableImmutableAdminUpgradeabilityProxy: its EIP-1967 implementation slot held 0x2d5bc0f897ad211ef9f954eadf59c43fb1ec4788 continuously over a 25-point probe of [15927425, 21120284] and that implementation's runtime is likewise constant. callTracer on the exploit tx shows three further delegatecall targets from the pool's context: 0x10ea06d74f8d7681f584558d9200cc7a9b852a9f and 0xf25d23913c6c8de1c3c25539fdabee1e51a06c63 are link-time libraries (runtime begins 73<self>3014) with constant code, and 0x85b79018c781b499f2878bee14e4e8b5db31ac61 is the LendingPoolCollateralManager, which is NOT hardcoded - it is resolved through the addresses provider 0xA91B9095eFa6C0568467562032202108e49c9Ef8. Binary-searching eth_call of getLendingPoolCollateralManager() over the same range shows it set once, at block 15927451 (2021-05-07T09:18:35Z, 135 s after the proxy's creation) and never changed before the incident, so the deployment basis stands.

incident.name: AIC reserve-mismatch skim
incident.notes: AIC fee-on-transfer accounting let repeated AIC/NEX cycles inflate the pair's untracked AIC surplus, which the attacker extracted through the public skim() function.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim creator 0x13b81c2e8a4edd2aac1a096889b778103b16f7e8 via 0x00b3fde6a293c628c0a23db5fb0aef2e2e033a5e146e8def94f9efa8ad1d57b2; not attacker

incident.name: AIDC pair-side accumulated burn
incident.notes: AIDCToken lets an ordinary router transfer burn the accumulated sell-side amount directly out of the AIDC/WBNB pair and then sync it, so repeated fresh-helper sells deflated the pair's AIDC reserve and let the attacker buy the pool out.

incident.name: AIRBTC helper unauthenticated process()
incident.notes: The AIRBTC helper's process(address,address) is unauthenticated and swaps a caller-chosen token pair using the contract's own balances, so the attacker directed it against the PandaToken/BSC-USD path and took the output.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim 0x12050e4355a392162698c6cf30eb8c9e0777300d created 2024-08-30T11:06:14Z by 0xd4596e984c50a74b6ba0e7f7ce10c3a182e0e3e2, which is not the attack-tx sender 0xcc116696f9852c238a5c8d3d96418ddba02357fc; 0 EIP-1967 Upgraded events on the victim before the incident; code age measured from deployment (onchain).

incident.name: AIRWA public setBurnRate()
incident.notes: AIRWA.setBurnRate(uint256) has no owner check, so the attacker set the burn rate to 98%, triggered it with a zero-value transfer to the LP to destroy the pair's AIRWA, reset it and sold into the inflated price.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim 0x3af7da38c9f68df9549ce1980eef4ac6b635223a created 2025-04-03T16:12:26Z by 0xe16f74bf9bb4b8670bc4d39b8cc4abfae3b2a421, which is not the attack-tx sender 0x70f0406e0a50c53304194b2668ec853d664a3d9c; 0 EIP-1967 Upgraded events on the victim before the incident; code age measured from deployment (onchain). 56.73 BNB x $591.44/BNB at the incident timestamp 1743733985 (DefiLlama coingecko:binancecoin) = $33,552.

incident.name: Akutars auction processRefunds() unbounded refund loop
incident.lossOther: 11,539.5 ETH permanently locked in the auction contract
incident.notes: processRefunds() refunded bidders in a single loop with a push transfer, and claimProjectFunds() required the refund cursor to reach the end, so one bidding contract that rejected ETH permanently blocked both functions and locked every bid in the contract.

sources.ref: onchain review: AkuAuction 0xF42c318dbfBaab0EEE040279C6a2588Fa01a961d created 2022-04-22T20:32:27Z by 0xcc0ecd808ce4fed81f0552b3889656b28aa2bae9 (the project owner), unrelated to the tx sender; no EIP-1967 events, age from deployment - 15,262 seconds (4.2 hours) old when the auction closed. This is a griefing/denial-of-service bug with no attacker profit: 11,539.5 ETH x $2,960.64 at incidentTimestamp 1650674809 (DefiLlama) = $34,164,388 of bids frozen, not stolen.

incident.name: Alkemi Earn self-liquidation collateral inflation
incident.notes: AlkemiEarn.liquidateBorrow() let a borrower liquidate their own position with the borrowed asset also serving as the collateral asset, crediting more supply than the repayment consumed, so a flash-loaned supply/borrow/self-liquidate/withdraw sequence walked out with more ETH than was deposited.

sources.ref: onchain review: AlkemiEarn proxy 0x4822D9172e5b76b9Db37B75f5552F9988F98a888 created 2021-09-07T18:41:12Z by 0x520da6e55eb070aa872cd08fe2665da44535cd33, not the attack-tx sender 0x0ed1c01b8420a965d7bd2374db02896464c91cd7; two EIP-1967 Upgraded events, the last at block 13685518 on 2021-11-25T20:14:20Z installing 0x85a948fd70b2b415bda93324581fb5fff1293df7, so the executing code was 1565.7 days old. 43.45 ETH x $2,055.46 at the incident timestamp (DefiLlama) = $89,310.

incident.name: Allbridge CCTP phantom deposit
incident.notes: CCTPTokenMessenger credited an attested generic Circle message from its untrusted body without verifying a USDC mint or recipient, enabling a phantom deposit to pass the Router's solvency check.

incident.name: Allbridge BSC pool spot-price manipulation
incident.notes: The swap pool behaved as designed; after flash-loaning enough BUSD/USDT to become effectively the sole liquidity provider, the attacker used swaps to skew the pool's own balance-ratio price and then deposited and withdrew against that skewed spot price to extract more than was put in.

sources.ref: onchain review: pool proxy 0x312bc7eaaf93f1c60dc5afc115fccde161055fb0 created 2022-04-18 by 0x8c6644415b3f3cd7fc0a453c5be3d3306fe0b2f9 (Allbridge deployer), unrelated to attack sender 0xc578d755cd56255d3ff6e92e1b6371ba945e3984; 1 EIP-1967 Upgraded event on 2022-08-31 to implementation 0x2c3c340233338d875637304b06f4f6faf9bebd20, giving a 213-day code age; separate from the 2026 Allbridge CCTP incident already in this dataset (different chain and contract)

incident.name: VUN public _swap arbitrary router call
incident.notes: VUN's internal _swap(address,bytes) was left public, so any caller could make the vault execute an arbitrary 1inch unoswapTo call and route the vault's ALP_APO holdings to itself before redeeming them.

incident.name: Ambient CrocSwapDex surplus-collateral accounting
incident.notes: Flash-loaned WETH deposited as CrocSwapDex native surplus collateral, then a tick-by-tick walk of the ETH/USDC curve with a narrow mint-and-harvest let the attacker disburse more surplus than was deposited, exposing a surplus-collateral accounting flaw in the dex.

sources.ref: onchain review: CrocSwapDex 0xAaAaAAAaA24eEeb8d57D431224f73832bC34f688 created 2023-05-29 by 0x8023901399d7927181892642a0913b06fda30847, unrelated to attack sender; the dex declares only CrocKnockoutCross and emits no EIP-1967 Upgraded event, so code changes were recovered by binary-searching eth_getStorageAt over proxyPaths_ (address[65536] at slot 1, callpath k at slot 1+k) between the creation and incident blocks: callpaths 0/2/3/4/7 installed 2023-05-29, callpath 1 reinstalled 2024-02-26T23:12:47Z (block 19314934, WarmPath 0xa9dd587ad17aed82cac5596b16dcc9defec885cb) and callpath 5 2024-02-26T23:33:35Z (block 19315038); callpaths 6/8-12/128-133 unset. The exploit drives callpaths 1, 2 and 3. Age measured from the latest install rather than deployment; ~67.85 ETH extracted

incident.documentedLastChange: 2024-02-26T23:33:35Z (block 19315038): last CrocSwapDex callpath sidecar install before the incident; the WarmPath sidecar carrying surplus-collateral accounting (callpath 1) was reinstalled 21 minutes earlier at 2024-02-26T23:12:47Z, block 19314934

incident.name: ANCH token pair-balance skim
incident.notes: The ANCH token's transfer logic moves tokens out of the liquidity pair's own balance without calling sync(), so the attacker repeatedly skim()ed the surplus and swapped it against the pair's USDT.

sources.ref: onchain review: ANCH 0xA4f5d4aFd6b9226b3004dD276A9F778EB75f2e9e created 2022-07-22T07:42:43Z by 0xb8a03ef93bc5354c14c385f35a296fd4c34e47ad, unrelated to attack sender 0x7f2f5212bb279c228363b085abf8a689f3475b15; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, age measured from deployment. No published loss figure, so lossUsd is a conservative onchain bound: the ANCH/USDT pair 0xaD0dA05b9C20fa541012eE2e89AC99A864CC68Bb held 33,144.54 USDT at block 20302530 and 16,900.91 USDT at block 20303000 as the skim was repeated, i.e. 16,243.64 USDT drained in the first minutes of the attack (the balance kept falling to 3,724.69 USDT by block 20340000).

incident.name: Ankr (aBNBc)
incident.notes: Compromised deployer key upgraded the aBNBc token to a version with unrestricted mint. Key compromise (the code change itself was the attack).

incident.notes: The Annex Liquidator's PancakeSwap flash-swap callback never verified that msg.sender was a legitimate factory pair, so the attacker created a pair for a worthless self-minted token and had it call the liquidator, draining its WBNB.

incident.notes: The TransSwap proxy priced APC against MUSD from the APC pair's live reserves, so a flash loan pumped APC, swapped it into MUSD at the inflated rate and swapped back once the price had been dumped.

incident.lossOther: 60,564 APE claimed with flash-loaned BAYC NFTs
incident.notes: The ApeCoin airdrop contract paid out against current BAYC/MAYC ownership instead of a pre-announced snapshot, so the attacker flash-loaned five BAYC out of the NFTX vault, claimed 60,564 APE for them and returned the NFTs in the same transaction.

incident.name: ApeDAO

incident.notes: APEMAGA.family(address) had no access control and reduced the target's token balance, so calling it three times against the Uniswap V2 pair and then sync() collapsed the pair's APEMAGA reserve and let the attacker's small pre-bought position be sold for the pool's WETH.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim created 2025-12-15 by 0xbeef63ae5a2102506e8a352a5bb32aa8b30b3112 (not the attacker), no EIP-1967 Upgraded event before the incident. Reported incident total $3.67M across Ethereum/Arbitrum/Base.

incident.name: ARA

incident.name: Balancer STA deflationary-token pool drain
incident.notes: The BPool credited swapExactAmountIn with the requested tokenAmountIn instead of the amount actually received, and exposed a permissionless gulp() that resyncs a token's recorded balance to the real one, so repeatedly swapping the 1%-transfer-fee token STA and calling gulp drove the pool's recorded STA balance to 1 wei and let 1 STA be swapped out for essentially the whole WETH side - the pool's own accounting, not any external price, is what failed.

sources.ref: onchain review: BPool 0x0e511aa1a137aad267dfe3a6bfca0b856c1a3682 (STA/WETH) was created 2020-05-29T13:57:13Z at block 10160718 by 0x43189898d712df36d37c41d2897843482f729c65 through BFactory 0x9424b1412450d0f8fc2255faf6046b98213b76bd, unrelated to attack sender 0xbf675c80540111a310b06e1482f9127ef4e7469a or its attack contract 0x81d73c55458f024cdc82bbf27468a2deaa631407. Loss not recorded in USD: the pool's WETH balance fell from 455.924127 to 0.077179 WETH inside the transaction (455.85 WETH taken). Order-of-magnitude sanity check only (ETH ~ $225 in June 2020, so ~$0.1m): far above the $1,000 floor. incident.name: BEC batchTransfer integer overflow
incident.lossOther: 2 x 5.79e76 BEC minted from nothing; exchanges halted BEC and the token's market value collapsed

sources.ref: onchain review: BunniHub 0x0000...65f1 (creator 0xfbe09b7a6c6cc3a72b4ca41cdd9c88ac62bb7937, unrelated to attack sender 0x0c3d8fa7...) is reached through Uniswap v4 PoolManager and BunniHook 0x000052423c1db6b7ff8641b85a7eefc7b2791888 in the attack tx; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events before the incident; the identical Unichain deployment (same address, deployed 2025-06-11) was drained 171 seconds earlier and is omitted here only because scripts/verify.mjs has no chain id for unichain. incident.name: bZx Fulcrum ETHDenver flash-loan margin trade
incident.notes: iTokens_loanOpeningFunctions.takeOrderFromiToken guarded the collateral check with a short-circuiting OR - require((loanDataBytes.length == 0 && sentAmounts[6] == sentAmounts[1]) || !OracleInterface(oracle).shouldLiquidate(...)) - so with empty loanDataBytes the left operand was true and shouldLiquidate() was never called, letting a 5x short open against the iETH pool that was instantly underwater after 5,637 ETH was swapped into 51 WBTC on Uniswap V1.

sources.ref: onchain review: the exploit path is attacker contract 0x4f4e0f2cb72e718fc0433222768c57e823162152 -> iETH LoanToken 0x77f973fcaf871459aa58cd81881ce453759281bc (marginTradeFromDeposit, selector 0x1c5d1da5) -> BZxProxy 0x1cf226e9413addaf22412a2e182f9c0de44af002 (takeOrderFromiToken, selector 0xb1eac3ad), which DELEGATECALLs the iTokens_loanOpeningFunctions module 0xf0a42ec4ebb7664af5dae5c3209345d545da838a carrying the skipped shouldLiquidate check. BZxProxy was created 2019-01-28 by 0xadff3ada12ed0f8a87e31e5a04dfd2ee054e1118 (bZx deployer), unrelated to attack sender 0x148426fdc4c8a51b96b4bed827907b5fa6491ad0. BZxProxy is a per-selector module registry (mapping(bytes4 => address) targets) that emits no EIP-1967 Upgraded event, so module installs were recovered by calling targets(bytes4) under binary search over block height: targets(0xb1eac3ad) first held 0xfbc580e4f16234d5783314f1d4195971eff453f4 and was rewritten to 0xf0a42ec4 at block 9443140 (2020-02-08T16:24:12Z, tx 0x7e49e3da0817322d9a118957fd535e10ae9e19e0022181d227f01e9b7c6d3d5f from the bZx deployer via settings contract 0xbb536eb24fb89b544d4bd9e9f1f34d9fd902bb96); the other selectors the exploit drives were installed earlier (targets(0x327ab639) 2019-08-08, targets(0xb1fd9e05) 2019-12-06), so the flawed module is also the most recent install and sets the age at 6.39d rather than the 3.16y deployment figure. bZx replaced this module three days later - the same selector resolves to 0x3756fa458880fa8fe53604101cf31c542ef22f6f in the 2020-02-18 transaction. Loss not recorded in USD: the attacker took 71.4 ETH directly (6.41 ETH left in 0x4f4e0f2c plus 64.97 ETH forwarded to the EOA) and left an unrepaid Compound position worth ~1,200 ETH, the 1,271 ETH figure reported everywhere; the iETH pool's WETH balance fell from 4,858.74 to 160.72 WETH inside the transaction, leaving the undercollateralized loan behind. Order-of-magnitude sanity check only (ETH ~ $265 in Feb 2020, so ~$0.3m): far above the $1,000 floor.
loss converted at the incident timestamp (1581730737) via DefiLlama coins: 1,271 ETH x $279.72 = $355,522

incident.name: bZx sUSD Kyber spot-price manipulation
incident.notes: The BZxOracle priced collateral off Kyber's getExpectedRate; the attacker bought sUSD from the Synthetix depot at ~$1 and then pushed the Kyber sUSD/ETH spot rate above $2 through the Uniswap and Synthetix reserves, so the oracle returned a doubled sUSD value and the protocol lent 6,796 ETH against it - the contracts behaved exactly as written, only the consumed price was wrong.

sources.ref: onchain review: the transaction goes attacker EOA 0xb8c6ad5fe7cb6cc72f2c4196dca11fbb272a8cbf -> iETH LoanToken 0x77f973fcaf871459aa58cd81881ce453759281bc flashBorrowToken (0x66fa576f) -> attacker contract 0x360f85f0b74326cddff33a812b05353bc537747b, which round-trips sUSD through the Synthetix depot 0x172e09691dfbbc035e37c73b62095caa16ee2388 and 19 Kyber trades before borrowing; the price the borrow is sized against is read by BZxOracle 0xaa6198fe597dfc331471ae7deba026fb299297fc, which STATICCALLs Kyber 0x818e6fecd516ecc3849daf6845e3ec868087b755 getExpectedRate (0x809a9e55) six times. That oracle was created 2020-02-17T00:55:43Z (block 9498957) by 0xadff3ada12ed0f8a87e31e5a04dfd2ee054e1118, the bZx deployer, unrelated to the attack sender - it is the replacement oracle bZx shipped after the 2020-02-15 incident, in use for 20.97 hours before this one. It is a plain non-proxy contract: no DELEGATECALL appears in the exploit trace and its codehash is identical (0xdb972a7db9bbcc6b4131490943344fac3aaa3e67836e7553135861350e2bc869) at its creation block and at the incident block, so the age is measured from deployment. Classified oracle-manipulation, not code-bug: the flaw is in trusting a manipulable Kyber spot rate, not in bZx's own logic. Loss not recorded in USD: attacker contract 0x360f85f0 held 0 ETH before the transaction and 2,378.153715 ETH after, while the iETH pool's WETH balance fell from 18,586.28 to 11,787.02 WETH. Order-of-magnitude sanity check only (ETH ~ $270 in Feb 2020, so ~$0.6m): far above the $1,000 floor.
loss converted at the incident timestamp (1581995638) via DefiLlama coins: 2,378 ETH x $268.14 = $637,640

incident.name: bZx iETH self-transfer duplication
incident.notes: LoanTokenLogic's _internalTransferFrom cached the sender and receiver balances before writing them and never rejected _from == _to, so each self-transfer of iETH credited the receiver without debiting the sender and doubled the attacker's iETH before burnToEther().

incident.name: CAROL Protocol sell() reentrancy on ethReserved
incident.notes: CAROLProtocol.sell() routed the payout through swapExactTokensForETH, which calls the seller's receive() before the contract's ethReserved bookkeeping is finalised, so re-entering from that callback let a bond position funded by chained flash loans be sold against a manipulated reserve figure.

incident.name: Cone Vault malicious implementation adminMint
incident.notes: Concentric's deployer wallet was social-engineered and the attacker used its proxy-admin rights to point the Cone Vault proxies at implementation 0xf36c407f3c467e9364ac1b2486aa199751ba177d, which added a backdoor adminMint() that burns LP from the staking contract and mints vault shares to the caller plus withdrawFromAdmin() to pull any balance still approved to the vault.

sources.ref: onchain review: attack tx calls Cone Vault V1 WETH/USDC proxy 0x8883d82e852f966ce88a9a9917d70d6f9e3933d9 with selector 0xc1f26123 (adminMint) from EOA 0x105f52fcc329cef4cbe25bc946f8a3738414e4a1; the proxy was created 2023-11-03 by 0xeaf6e2a3d22a9775a1cc692b207b7d8dd6a4944c, not by the attacker. It is an EIP-173-style proxy that emits no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, so the malicious upgrade is invisible to the mechanical measurement and the age is measured from deployment - flagged nonStandardUpgradeArchitecture. Tier-1 measurement: the hardhat-deploy EIP-173 proxy does emit its own ProxyImplementationUpdated(address,address) event (topic 0x5570d70a002632a7b0b3c9304cc89efb62d8da9eca0dbd7752c83b7379068296); eth_getLogs over [creation 146573591, incident 172948936] returns exactly two - 0x0 -> 0x8b85b292be63e4c3592ecf09b5500575037018e0 at deployment (block 146573591, 2023-11-03T02:47:32Z) and 0x8b85b292... -> 0xf36c407f3c467e9364ac1b2486aa199751ba177d at block 172948684 (2024-01-22T07:55:43Z, tx 0x6266b5d3ff0a8d366ac9d9470a3215e8ab0ac3dc4992b2d5381e059254b04737), i.e. the attacker's backdoor implementation was installed 64 seconds before the drain, so the exploited code was 64 seconds old rather than 80 days.

incident.documentedLastChange: 2024-01-22T07:55:43Z (block 172948684, tx 0x6266b5d3ff0a8d366ac9d9470a3215e8ab0ac3dc4992b2d5381e059254b04737): the malicious upgrade itself - ProxyImplementationUpdated(address,address) (topic 0x5570d70a002632a7b0b3c9304cc89efb62d8da9eca0dbd7752c83b7379068296) emitted by the vault proxy 0x8883d82e852f966ce88a9a9917d70d6f9e3933d9, moving the implementation from 0x8b85b292be63e4c3592ecf09b5500575037018e0 to the backdoored 0xf36c407f3c467e9364ac1b2486aa199751ba177d, 64 seconds before the adminMint() drain

incident.name: Conic
incident.notes: Read-only reentrancy on Curve remove_liquidity skews GenericOracle LP prices used by the ETH omnipool.

sources.ref: Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the ETH omnipool is not a proxy (no EIP-1967 implementation or beacon slot) and its own runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 17592111 and the incident block 17740955, but ConicEthPool executes two external handlers by DELEGATECALL - controller.curveHandler() and controller.convexHandler() (Address.functionDelegateCall at ConicEthPool.sol lines 277/290/461/470) - so its executing code can be repointed from the immutable Controller 0x013A3Da6591d3427F164862793ab4e388F9B587e. Binary-searching eth_getStorageAt on the Controller shows curveHandler (slot 6) changed at block 17613432, 2023-07-03T12:26:23Z (timestamp 1688387183), from 0x92bffb71bbe241ba9cdfb3a4e56e48dc4f118ed7 to 0xD775ae26F89bcd89e66485324D8830c0EF1e8B6c, corroborated by the Controller's own CurveHandlerSet(address) log (topic 0x40f17cc99608acc0aa583a98bd741564e79111d55e65adc0399f400a707d4831, data 0x...d775ae26) in tx 0x0b1dfe6ee755dc11a9a0d0823e22abcc0cb1f03e5ed0673c1f68183cf84f58e6, sent by the Conic deployer 0xc0f0c674dcf195e2c39dfa7bb59fa968b7f7c575 through the governance proxy 0xcb7c67bdde9f7af0667e8d82bb87f1432bd1d902 - a protocol action, not the attacker's; convexHandler (slot 7) held 0x635228EDAEAd8a76b6ae1779bd7682043321943D unchanged over the same range, and the new curveHandler 0xD775ae26F89bcd89e66485324D8830c0EF1e8B6c (created block 17591566 by the pool's own deployer 0xedaeb101f34d767f263c0fe6b8d494e3d071f0ba) has no DELEGATECALL and identical code from its install to the incident. The last change to the executing code is therefore the curveHandler swap, not the pool deployment: lastChangeTimestamp 1688387183, codeAgeSeconds 1689935711-1688387183 = 1548528 (17.92 d instead of 20.92 d). For completeness the Controller's priceOracle (slot 8) was also repointed twice in the window, last at block 17634814 (2023-07-06T12:29:35Z) to GenericOracle 0x286eF89cD2DA6728FD2cb3e1d1c5766Bcea344b0 - the feed the read-only reentrancy skews - but that oracle is reached by CALL, not DELEGATECALL, so it is not part of the victim's executing code and is not used as the basis.

incident.documentedLastChange: 2023-07-03T12:26:23Z (block 17613432): Conic Controller 0x013A3Da6591d3427F164862793ab4e388F9B587e setCurveHandler -> CurveHandlerSet(0xD775ae26F89bcd89e66485324D8830c0EF1e8B6c), storage slot 6, tx 0x0b1dfe6ee755dc11a9a0d0823e22abcc0cb1f03e5ed0673c1f68183cf84f58e6; the ETH omnipool DELEGATECALLs this handler, so it is part of the victim's executing code

incident.name: Conic crvUSD omnipool spot-price sandwich
incident.notes: crvUSD omnipool values LP deposits/withdrawals via manipulable Curve pool spot prices sandwiched by attacker.

sources.ref: Onchain review: crvUSD omnipool 0x369cbc5c6f139b1132d3b91b87241b37fc5b971f created 2023-06-08T18:00:59Z (block 17438004) by 0xedaeb101f34d767f263c0fe6b8d494e3d071f0ba, unrelated to the attack sender 0xb6369f59fc24117b16742c9dfe064894d03b3b80. The pool is not itself a proxy (implementation() reverts; Etherscan's Proxy flag is a false positive) and its keccak(eth_getCode) is identical at the creation and incident blocks, but _depositToCurvePool/_withdrawFromCurvePool run `controller.curveHandler().functionDelegateCall(...)` and `controller.convexHandler().functionDelegateCall(...)`, so part of the executing code is fetched from the Controller at call time. Reading the Controller's storage rather than any event: slot 6 (curveHandler) changed 0x92bffb71bbe241ba9cdfb3a4e56e48dc4f118ed7 -> 0xd775ae26f89bcd89e66485324d8830c0ef1e8b6c at block 17613432 (2023-07-03T12:26:23Z), and slot 7 (convexHandler, 0x635228edaead8a76b6ae1779bd7682043321943d) never changed over [17438004, 17743469]. Both handlers appear as delegatecall targets of the victim in the exploit trace. Age measured from the curveHandler swap: 18.3 days rather than the 42.9 days the deployment basis gave.

incident.documentedLastChange: 2023-07-03T12:26:23Z (block 17613432): the Conic Controller 0x013A3Da6591d3427F164862793ab4e388F9B587e had its curveHandler (controller storage slot 6) changed 0x92bffb71bbe241ba9cdfb3a4e56e48dc4f118ed7 -> 0xd775ae26f89bcd89e66485324d8830c0ef1e8b6c; the omnipool executes that handler's code in its own context via Address.functionDelegateCall, so this is a change of the victim's executing code

incident.name: Cover Protocol Blacksmith stale-cache infinite mint
incident.notes: Blacksmith cached the Pool struct in memory, then called updatePool() which wrote the new accRewardsPerToken to storage, and afterwards computed the miner's rewardWriteoff from the stale in-memory value, leaving the writeoff far too low so subsequent claims minted effectively unbounded COVER.

incident.notes: The crYUSD market priced its collateral from yUSD's pricePerFullShare, which the attacker doubled by donating the underlying Curve LP directly into the yUSD vault, so the same yUSD collateral supported twice the borrowing power - the market itself behaved as written.

sources.ref: onchain review: crYUSD 0x4BAa77013ccD6705ab0522853cB0E9d453579Dd4 created 2021-06-01T02:56:49Z by 0x197939c1ca20c2b506d6811d8b6cdb3394471074, unrelated to the attack sender 0x24354d31...; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events between creation and the incident (Cream cTokens change implementation through the Comptroller's own _setImplementation, and none fired for this market), so age runs from deployment: 1635342850 - 1622516209 = 12,826,641 s (148.5 days). re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis. Slot 18 held 0x1c8645bec146ae9a3489fc5821b69c9191577331 at all 25 sample points across [12546046, 13499798]; the only NewImplementation(address,address) on the market is the 0x0 -> 0x1c8645be write in its creation block; and callTracer on the exploit tx shows the market delegatecalling only that implementation, which has zero DELEGATECALL opcodes. sources.ref: onchain review (no exploit tx: incident block located by binary-searching eth_getBlockByNumber to measurement.incidentTimestamp -> ethereum block 17805708, 2023-07-30T12:00:00Z). incident.name: Curve LlamaLend sDOLA-long2 oracle manipulation
incident.notes: The sDOLA-long2 market's CryptoFromPoolVaultWAgg oracle priced collateral as p_collateral * sDOLA.convertToAssets(1e18), an atomically manipulable spot share rate, so a flash-loaned mass redemption of ~10.6M sDOLA crashed the reported collateral value and let the attacker hard-liquidate 27 solvent borrowers.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim 0xaD444663... is the LlamaLend 'crvUSD Controller' created 2025-03-19 by 0xf7bd34dd44b92fb2f9c3d2e31aaad06570a853a6 (not the attacker), no Upgraded events; collateral_token() returns sDOLA 0xb45ad160634c528Cc3D2926d9807104FA3157305 and its AMM 0x0079885E248B572CdC4559A8B156745e2d8EA1f7 reports price_oracle_contract() 0x88822eE517Bfe9A1b97bf200b0b6D3F356488fF2. Curve's post-mortem puts seized borrower equity at ~$822K and attacker net at ~$245K; DARKNAVY measures attacker profit at $240,567 across 27 liquidated borrowers. Also reported as an Inverse Finance / DOLA incident.

re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis. The pool is Vyper and its runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 22083746 and the incident block 24566937; the two 0xf4 bytes a naive scan flags are at pc 21831/21928 of 22709, inside the trailing data/immutables region. callTracer on the exploit tx shows 58 frames executing the pool's own code and zero DELEGATECALL out of its context, so the executing code is the pool's own and cannot be repointed.

incident.name: DAO Maker vesting unprotected init()
incident.notes: The vesting contract's init() carried no access control or initialized guard, so the attacker re-initialized it with themselves as the sole beneficiary and then called emergencyExit() to sweep the deposited sale tokens.

sources.ref: onchain review: attack tx calls 0x2fd602ed directly with selector 0x84304ad7 (init); contract created 2021-08-03 by 0xcf28556ee95be8c52ad2f3480149128cca51dac1, not by attack sender 0x2708cace; note this is the 2021-09-03 DAO Maker incident, distinct from the 2021-08-12 one. incident.name: DEI token burnFrom reversed allowance lookup
incident.notes: The DEI implementation deployed on 2023-04-16 wrote the allowance update inside burnFrom() with the owner and spender arguments transposed, so calling burnFrom(victim, 0) granted the caller an unlimited allowance over the victim and let the attacker transferFrom every DEI holder that had ever approved the token.

incident.name: Dexible v2 selfSwap arbitrary router call
incident.notes: Dexible v2's selfSwap() forwarded a caller-supplied router address and calldata without an allowlist, so the attacker pointed it at ERC20 contracts and had Dexible transferFrom the balances of every wallet still holding an approval to it.

sources.ref: onchain review: Dexible v2 0xDE62E1b0edAa55aAc5ffBE21984D321706418024 created 2023-02-15T17:31:47Z by 0xb631e8650fb4befdae74ab9f86a9cb65bc134706, unrelated to the attack sender; no EIP-1967 events, age from deployment - only 125,328 seconds (1.45 days) old at the incident. The recorded tx is the TRU leg the PoC replays; the ~$2M figure is PeckShield's total across all drained approvals. Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): DexibleProxy is a custom timelocked proxy that keeps its logic pointer in the diamond-style slot ProxyStorage.DATA_KEY 0x21b00fb42ba9970a2143fc9fb216ce19c58db008c8d83ff3a715bbc79598d7f0, not in an EIP-1967 slot; a binary search of eth_getStorageAt on that slot over [16635649, 16646023] shows it holds 0x33e690aea97e4ef25f0d140f1bf044d663091daf packed with the 604800-second timelock, unchanged from creation to the incident (the proposeUpgrade/upgradeLogic path was never used), and the logic contract - created one block before the proxy by the same deployer - is byte-identical over the window and contains no DELEGATECALL of its own, so the 1.45-day age is measured from the right point.

incident.name: DFX Finance Curve flash() reentrancy
incident.notes: Curve.flash() was the only state-changing entry point without the contract's nonReentrant guard, so the attacker re-entered deposit() inside flashCallback and had the flash-loaned XIDR/USDC counted both as flash repayment and as a new LP deposit, then withdrew the underlying.

sources.ref: onchain review: verified Curve source on 0x46161158b1947d9149e066d6d31af1283b2d377c - every other mutating function carries nonReentrant, flash() does not; victim created by 0xa75ceb6801d48449affa0ee6f31205b2a5567bec (DFX deployer) in tx 0xdf81dad568a455c860bfd7defb2861a4699b896e31c6c1c49836cd5bb10362fb, unrelated to attack sender 0x14c19962e4a899f29b3dd9ff52ebfb5e4cb9a067; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events before the incident. Of the code executed in its context during the exploit, the Swaps library 0x5fca000f8a1ef45fe2412a8e305ff36d8757be0f is a PUSH20 link-time constant in the runtime, and the two assimilators it delegatecalls, 0x08cd9d993840cca86546f4ebf166c78c7d8ff700 and 0xc2e645c253faf984b6af2668798719b7c6abab95, live in curve.assets[0] and [1] (slots keccak(4) and keccak(4)+1); binary-searching eth_getStorageAt on both over [15747623, 15941703] shows they were written at deployment and never changed.

incident.name: DODO DVM re-callable init()

incident.name: DOGGO self-balance-triggered swapback sandwich
incident.notes: DOGGO's transfer hook fired an internal, slippage-free Uniswap sale of the token's own accumulated fee balance whenever balanceOf(DOGGO) crossed a hard-coded 4.2069e18 threshold, and because anyone can donate tokens to the contract the attacker controlled exactly when that sale fired and sandwiched it inside a flash loan.

incident.name: DolomiteMarginProtocol callFunction approval drain
incident.notes: The retired Ethereum DolomiteMarginProtocol exposed callFunction(), which performs an arbitrary external call and is protected only by a noEntry reentrancy modifier that can be bypassed by entering through the unguarded SoloMargin operate path, letting the attacker make the contract transferFrom USDC out of every wallet that still held a stale approval to it.

incident.name: DPC staking reward miscalculation
incident.notes: DPC.claimStakeLp() recomputed the LP staking reward from the caller's current stake on every call instead of accruing it over elapsed time, so repeated claims in the same day paid the reward many times over.

sources.ref: onchain review: DPC 0xB75cA3C3e99747d0e2F6e75A9fBD17F5Ac03cebE created 2022-09-07T09:14:55Z by 0x8e59424663e6ba2327564b28437b6e0294a4725c, unrelated to attack sender 0xf211fa86cbc60d693d687075b03dff3c225b25c9; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, age measured from deployment. The attack ran as a long series of small claims from 0x2109bbecB0a563e204985524Dd3DB2F6254AB419 and 0xf211fa86cbc60d693d687075b03dff3c225b25c9 (this transaction alone drained 547.75 USDT from the DPC pair); lossUsd uses the ~$103,755 total reported by Beosin. Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the victim sets no EIP-1967 implementation or beacon slot and its runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 21120156 and the incident block 21179552; all ten DELEGATECALL sites are solc external-library calls to the PUSH20 constant 0xff7a90fa8193b51482c37e84f3e9a0798921380b (with the usual EXTCODESIZE guard), a library deployed five blocks before the victim by the same creator 0x8e59424663e6ba2327564b28437b6e0294a4725c and byte-identical over the window, so the target is fixed.

incident.name: DRLVaultV3
incident.notes: DRLVault.swapToWETH traded through the USDC/WETH pool with no effective slippage guard, so the attacker sandwiched the vault after manipulating the pool price.

sources.ref: Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the victim is an EIP-1167 minimal-proxy clone whose 45-byte runtime hardcodes the master 0x8aa6b0e10bd6dbaf5159967f92f2e740afe2b4c3 (created at block 23731141), so the DELEGATECALL target cannot be repointed; the master's runtime is byte-identical at the clone's creation block 23767200 and the incident block 23769387 and contains no DELEGATECALL, so the 7.3-hour age is measured from the deployment of code that never changed.

sources.ref: re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis. The victim is a Compound Unitroller; comptrollerImplementation is storage slot 2 (named layout via `cast storage`). Exactly one NewImplementation(address,address) fires, at block 25390597 (2023-02-05T01:25:23Z), 246 s after the Unitroller's own creation at block 25390515 (1675560077) - it is the initial wiring of the same deployment session, preceded by the matching NewPendingImplementation pair. Slot 2 is constant at 0x55decf1b592b1b3ff8af3fe801b0780276d222bc from that block to the incident (25-point probe) and callTracer on the exploit tx shows the Unitroller delegatecalling only that address (zero DELEGATECALL opcodes of its own). The 246 s is 0.0008% of the 375-day age, so the measurement is left on the deployment basis.

incident.name: DUCKVADER buyTokens per-address cap bypass
incident.notes: DUCKVADER.buyTokens() handed out tokens against a per-address limit only, with no payment tied to the amount, so the attacker looped fresh helper contracts to claim the allowance many times over and dumped the result on Uniswap V2.

The PoC deploys a fresh AttackContract2 per buy, confirming the limit is per address. ~5 ETH x $1,914.19 at the incident timestamp (DefiLlama) = $9,571.

incident.name: DxSale

incident.name: DYNA staking reward business-logic flaw
incident.notes: DYNA spawns a StakingReward contract per holder and the sold-amount limit in transfer() can be bypassed by routing through those contracts, so the attacker pre-seeded 200 of them and later drained the pair.

incident.name: EFLeverVault flash-loan balance inflation
incident.notes: EFLeverVault priced shares off its own ETH balance and exposed an unguarded receiveFlashLoan() callback, so anyone could have Balancer flash-loan WETH into the vault and then withdraw far more ETH than they had deposited.

sources.ref: onchain review: EFLeverVault 0xe39fd820b58f83205db1d9225f28105971c3d309 created 2022-05-27T05:12:32Z by 0xbf58e21b232ceea012122dd1fd60daad5791aa2e, unrelated to the attack sender; plain contract, no EIP-1967 events, age from deployment. The recorded tx is the generalised front-runner 0x26bce6ec... that landed first and took the ~750 ETH; the original exploiter 0xdf31F4C8dC9548eb4c416Af26dC396A25FDE4D5F ran the same call in 0x160c5950a01b88953648ba90ec0a29b0c5383e055d35a7835d905c53a3dda01e in the same block. 750 ETH x $1,325.14 at incidentTimestamp 1665748727 (DefiLlama) = $993,853.

re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis. The vault's runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 14852275 and the incident block 15746200, and its 61 DELEGATECALL sites are solc external-library calls to the link-time SafeMath at 0x071108ad85d7a766b41e0f5e5195537a8fc8e74d (the address Etherscan reports as the linked library; its runtime begins 73<self>3014 and is constant across the window). callTracer on the exploit tx confirms that library is the only delegatecall target. The vault does expose an owner-only arbitrary `to.delegatecall(data)`, which can write storage but cannot change the vault's own runtime code, so it is not an upgrade mechanism.

incident.name: ElasticSwap exchange decay accounting
incident.notes: The ElasticSwap ELP exchange tracked internal x*y=k reserves separately from real ERC-20 balances to support rebasing tokens, and the 'decay' correction let an attacker donate into the pool and then redeem liquidity for more than was contributed.

sources.ref: onchain review: the exploit transaction the PoC cites resolves on Ethereum mainnet, not Avalanche as the PoC's fork suggests; ELP exchange 0x4ae1Da57f2d6b2E9a23d07e264Aa2B3bBCaeD19A created 2022-05-07T15:57:56Z by 0x1806c8c7993086f971bb6f605a5cd3e369e64ed6, not the attack-tx sender 0xbeadedbabed6a353c9caa4894aa7e5f883e32967; no EIP-1967 events, 219.4 days old. Loss $845k per the DeFiHackLabs 2022 index entry for this PoC.

re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis. The Exchange's runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 14730695 and the incident block 16172820, and its five DELEGATECALL sites are solc external-library calls to the link-time-hardcoded MathLib 0xe3c08c95aa81474f44bee23f8c45d470ddad37be (runtime begins 73<self>3014, constant across the window), so nothing about the executing code can be repointed. Flagged separately for a curator, not changed here: callTracer on the cited exploit tx never reaches 0x4ae1Da57...; the ELP exchange actually drained is 0xa0c5aa50ce3cc69b1c478d8235597bc0c51dfdab, another ElasticSwap `Exchange` created 2022-05-10T02:51:50Z (block 14746111), which would give 18,747,657 s (217.0 d) instead of 18,959,691 s (219.4 d).

onchain review: victim corrected from ELP exchange 0x4ae1Da57f2d6b2E9a23d07e264Aa2B3bBCaeD19A, which emits no logs at all in the cited exploit transaction, to the ElasticSwap Exchange actually drained, 0xa0c5aa50ce3cc69b1c478d8235597bc0c51dfdab, which emits 14 of that transaction's logs and is its top emitter. incident.name: Euler Finance
incident.notes: Euler main proxy: donateToReserves (eIP-14) skipped the liquidity check, enabling self-liquidation at a discount. Euler installs code as modules on the proxy (InstallerInstallModule), not via EIP-1967 Upgraded: the EToken module carrying donateToReserves went live onchain 2022-08-18T16:01:33Z, and the last module install of any kind before the exploit was 2023-01-06T16:25:59Z, which is what the age is measured from.

sources.ref: onchain review (RPC only): Euler main proxy 0x27182842E098f60e3D576794A5bFFb0777E025d3 created 2021-11-26T04:13:05Z at block 13687582; eth_getLogs for EIP-1967 Upgraded (topic 0xbc7cd75a20ee27fd9adebab32041f755214dbc6bffa90cc0225b39da2e5c2d3b) over [13687582, 16818931] returns 0 logs. Code changes go through the Installer module and are recorded by InstallerInstallModule(uint256 moduleId, address moduleImpl, bytes32 gitCommit) (topic 0x15fc136599039b272cb44c0ace0b099754f2656d1d52691b99c9e348662c805a) emitted by the proxy itself: 44 installs between creation and the incident. The last install strictly before the first exploit tx 0xc310a0affe2169d1f6feec1c63dbc7f7c62a887fa48795d327d4d2da2d6b111d (block 16817996, 2023-03-13T08:50:59Z) is moduleId 2000506 -> 0x89e8f69c302d352d37de10019a69df4f7f959bef at block 16348923, 2023-01-06T16:25:59Z (tx 0x000f80a4884b72ff3814f92b5eb594870b025bd7ae840d9d5df426c2f1f42235). The preceding installs are 2022-12-16T14:38:11Z moduleId 4 Governance -> 0xe83b69edfd12e477fe47152c0e1d65576b91a1cf, 2022-12-01T14:14:11Z moduleId 2000505, 2022-10-18T14:55:35Z moduleId 7 SwapHub -> 0xc57d9e4a688551d99645b49126e93589d4b478c8, 2022-08-31T14:53:51Z moduleId 2000504, 2022-08-18T16:01:33Z moduleId 500000 EToken -> 0xbb0d4bb654a21054af95456a3b29c63e8d1f4c0a (block 15365947). The previously recorded date 2022-07-28 (the eIP-14 vote) matches no onchain install: scanning the installed EToken implementations for the donateToReserves selector 0x36f022aa, it is absent from 0x2d2f24c7 (2021-11-29), 0x03601edc (2021-12-10), 0x1245f078 (2022-03-28), 0xee385a1e (2022-04-10) and 0x196fdd95 (2022-08-04) and first appears in 0xbb0d4bb654a21054af95456a3b29c63e8d1f4c0a installed 2022-08-18T16:01:33Z, so even the flaw-introducing change is 21 days later than the recorded date (measuring from it would give 17870307s / 206.8d). Age is measured from the last pre-incident install per the dataset rule. The two installs at 2023-03-13T10:05:23Z and 11:44:23Z (moduleIds 500000/500001 pointed at 486-byte stubs, gitCommit '0x1') are the post-exploit emergency shutdown; they fall after the 08:50:59Z exploit but before this row's noon incidentTimestamp and are excluded. Correction: 19699200s (228.0d) -> 5686441s (65.8d).

Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): FlooringPeriphery is deployed directly (Etherscan verifies the source at the victim address itself and no EIP-1967 implementation or beacon slot is set) and its runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 18719162 and the incident block 18802289; its two DELEGATECALL sites are both OpenZeppelin Address.functionDelegateCall, reachable only from Multicall - which passes address(this) - and from the UUPS upgradeToAndCall path, which the onlyProxy/__self check makes unreachable on a directly deployed logic contract, so the executing code is the victim's own unchanged runtime.

incident.name: Four.meme launchpad liquidity migration into pre-initialized pool
incident.notes: The launchpad's addLiquidity() migration did not check that the PancakeSwap V3 pool for the graduating token was still uninitialized, so the attacker created and initialized the pool at a manipulated sqrtPriceX96 beforehand and swapped out the BNB the launchpad then deposited.

sources.ref: onchain review of the BSC sequence: attacker contract creates+initializes the V3 pool in block 46555725 (tx 0x4235b006...), the Four.meme launchpad 0x5c9520...762b executes addLiquidity (selector 0x55110640) from its own operator 0x74d86638f359bdff6ec55d78a97f294747f8f5b3 in block 46555731 (tx 0xe0daa3bf...), attacker takes profit in block 46555732; launchpad creator 0xe096774fef711a0b28cb7bc9839b892bd5e2f603 is unrelated to the attacker

incident.name: FoxLpBondsPool spot-priced bond mint
incident.notes: FoxLpBondsPool priced a bond from a manipulable PancakeSwap spot quote before its own large swap changed the reserves, then minted an immediate unsupported FOX referral reward.

incident.name: FPR helper contracts public setAdmin
incident.notes: The FPR helper contracts exposed setAdmin(address) to any caller, so the attacker made themselves admin and used remaining(address,address) to sweep the contracts' FPR and LP holdings.

incident.name: FractalProtocol
incident.notes: Fractal vault deposit/compute/withdraw share-price accounting was manipulable within one tx by a flashloaned deposit, letting the attacker withdraw more USDC.e than deposited.

incident.name: Furucombo Proxy delegatecall context hijack
incident.notes: Proxy._exec() delegatecalled whitelisted handlers, and the Aave V2 handler in turn delegatecalled the Aave lending-pool proxy, so calling initialize() through that path wrote an attacker-controlled implementation into Furucombo's own storage and let the resulting evil contract pull every token users had approved to the Furucombo proxy.

sources.ref: onchain review: Furucombo Proxy 0x17e8ca1b created 2021-01-09 by 0xbcb909975715dc8fde643ee44b89e3fd6a35a259, not by attack sender 0xb624e2b1; victim/tx cross-checked against Coinspect learn-evm-attacks test/Business_Logic/Furucombo (loss there stated as $15m; rekt's leaderboard says $14m, used here). Recheck (deployment basis confirmed): the Proxy's EIP-1967 implementation slot was zero for its entire pre-incident life and only became 0x86765dde9304bea32f65330d266155c4fa0c4f04 at block 11940500 (2021-02-27T16:47:53Z) - the attacker's own setup transaction 0x6a14869266a1dcf3f51b102f44b7af7d0a56f1766e5b1908ac80a6a23dbaf449, sent by the same address 0xb624e2b10b84a41687caec94bdd484e48d76b212 19 minutes before the anchored tx - so that slot write is a consequence of the bug, not a pre-incident code change. The Proxy's own runtime keccak(eth_getCode) is identical at the creation block 11618386 and the incident block 11940588, so the exploited code is the deployed Proxy code and deployment is the right basis.

incident.name: Futureswap fee unit confused for basis points
incident.notes: The exchange computed a token-denominated fee (abs(delta) * feeRateWad / 1e18) and forwarded it to FeeManager.addFee(), which interpreted the value as a basis-point weight, so an oversized trade produced an absurd fee share that redeemed the pool's USDC.e and WETH inventory.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim proxy created 2021-10-13 by 0x5ed35ea85fad2f578685a4d8e404c12164ea516c (not the attacker); three EIP-1967 Upgraded events, the last on 2021-12-18 to implementation 0x010659727ad7716c239e206acd3ebee0fdc9e207, so the exploited code was ~4 years old. Attack-tx logs show 894,992.85 USDC.e and 68 WETH leaving the proxy against 496,500 USDC.e paid in. DefiLlama records $395,000 (FutureSwap, 2026-01-10, Arbitrum, Withdrawal Logic Flaw).

incident.name: GALA v2 dormant minter-role key compromise

incident.name: GMX v1
incident.notes: GMX v1 Vault (deployed 2021): cross-contract reentrancy let short-position accounting inflate GLP price before redemption. Aged-code counterexample - v1 code was ~4 years old.

sources.ref: onchain review (exploit tx now identified from the DeFiHackLabs PoC: 0x0b8cd648fb585bc3d421fc02150013eab79e211ef8d1c68100f2820ce90a4712, arbitrum block 355878385, 2025-07-09T12:22:28Z, sender 0xdf3340a436c27655ba62f8281565c9925c3a5221 -- the attacker's leveraged-long open; the sequence continues with keeper execution 0x28a000501ef8e3364b0e7f573256b04b87d9a8e8173410c869004b987bf0beef, decrease order 0x20abfeff0206030986b05422080dc9e81dbb53a662fbc82461a47418decc49af and keeper execution 0x1f00da742318ad1807b6ea8283bfe22b4a8ab0bc98fe428fbfe443746a4a7353). GMX v1 Vault 0x489ee077994B6658eAfA855C308275EAd8097C4A was created at arbitrum block 227091, 2021-08-31T07:35:06Z. It is not a proxy: the runtime bytecode contains zero DELEGATECALL opcodes, there is no EIP-1967 Upgraded event on it, and eth_getCode returns a byte-identical runtime at the creation block and at the incident block. The code therefore provably never changed and the deployment basis is exact (gov/timelock can only retune parameters and swap the external VaultUtils helper, which is configuration rather than a change of the victim's code). Aged-code counterexample: ~1408 days.

incident.name: GNUS Axelar ITS salt reuse unauthorized mint
incident.notes: The GNUS deployer key was leaked through a Discord compromise and reused the project's Axelar Interchain Token Service salt to register a same-ID token manager on Fantom, so minting worthless GNUS there made the ITS executor mint 500,000 canonical GNUS to the attacker on Ethereum, which was then sold into the Uniswap V2 GNUS/WETH pair.

sources.ref: onchain review: exploit tx emits Transfer(0x0 -> 0x548c63a6a7299ab54762e1bfa6b56c1b94c2a820, 500000 GNUS) on the token 0x614577036f0a024dbc1c88ba616b394dd65d105a; the tx is signed by the Axelar ITS executor 0xc77820eef59629fc8d88154977bc8de8a1b2f4ae, so the attacker EOA recorded here is the mint recipient that dumped into the pool in 0xe8a5780cc89d9115acf307da9e6fae68e8b3634a8b41c77d81e95edb9085a407. Token created 2024-02-20 by the GNUS deployer 0x1804deca63705e18edf04f242b325bcd54a8b463 (the wallet whose key leaked), not by the attacker; it is a Diamond, so facet changes emit no EIP-1967 Upgraded event and the age may be overstated. Tier-1 measurement: the diamond emits DiamondCut(...) rather than EIP-1967 Upgraded, and eth_getLogs over [creation 19269335, incident 19802980] returns 10 DiamondCut events - block 19269335 (2024-02-20, deployment cut), 19273203/19273274/19273280/19273284/19273286/19273329/19273367/19273421 (all 2024-02-21) and a final one at block 19762552 (2024-04-29T17:47:59Z, tx 0x5d1ca14aa4eb0ce2c6f953fe6f3856bfbecbfb0945ec9a8420fb61d8152d0808) that re-cut the ERC20 and mint/burn facets six days before the exploit, so the age is measured from that cut (5.65 days) instead of deployment (74.8 days).

incident.name: Legacy Pool collectInterestRepayment missing access control
incident.notes: The deprecated 2020 Pool's collectInterestRepayment(address,uint256) had no access control and executed USDC.transferFrom(from, pool, amount) for any address still holding a standing approval, so the attacker deposited 1,000 USDC, pulled a legacy depositor's USDC into the pool to inflate the share price, and withdrew the inflated balance.

sources.ref: callTracer review: the attack tx calls the legacy Pool 0x0689aa22...4B43 with deposit(uint256) 0xb6b55f25, collectInterestRepayment(address,uint256) 0x64de8a07 against victim 0x526C7665C5dd9cD7102C6d42D407a0d9DC1e431d, then withdraw(uint256) 0x2e1a7d4d four times; the Pool is Goldfinch's own 'TransparentProxy' created 2020-09-25 by 0xc840b3e21ff0eba77468ad450d868d4362cf67fe (not the attacker). It stores its implementation outside the EIP-1967 slot and signals changes with a custom event 0x5570d70a...8296, which fired only three times (blocks 10929405, 10948041, 10953821, all in Sep 2020) and always resolves to the same implementation 0x7dbe30fde1eca6856806ff14fc456ec6791c73fe, with none after — so the deployment-based age is not overstated in practice

deployment-basis recheck (storage, not events): contrary to the earlier note, this TransparentProxy does keep its implementation in the EIP-1967 slot 0x360894a1...2bbc, and the exploit tx's three DELEGATECALLs from the Pool all go to 0x7dbe30fde1eca6856806ff14fc456ec6791c73fe, exactly the value that slot holds. eth_getStorageAt returns 0x7dbe30fde1eca6856806ff14fc456ec6791c73fe at the creation block 10929405, at the incident block 23924517 and at all 41 evenly spaced samples in between, and the proxy runtime is byte-identical at both ends, so the Sep-2020 custom events did not move the implementation. Deployment remains the correct basis; 1894.2 days.

incident.name: Grim Finance GrimBoostVault depositFor reentrancy
incident.notes: GrimBoostVault.depositFor(token, amount, user) took the deposit token as a caller-supplied parameter and minted shares around an unguarded external transferFrom call, so the attacker passed its own contract as the token and re-entered depositFor from that callback, minting eight tranches of vault shares against a single SpiritSwap BTC/WFTM LP deposit before burning them all in withdrawAll to drain the vault.

sources.ref: Onchain review over plain JSON-RPC. Etherscan v2 does not serve Fantom, so the victim's creation was resolved with no explorer at all, by binary-searching eth_getCode against the archive endpoint https://rpc.fantom.network (https://rpc.ftm.tools is dead and the l2beat Fantom key is disabled): GrimBoostVault 0x660184CE8AF80e0B1e5A1172A16168b15f4136bF first has code at block 15934352 (deployTimestamp 1630366055 = 2021-08-30T23:27:35Z), creation tx 0x163c49f8dcfc3c3242f6ff30b64445497b808c46e2f2c0e85c433314b678d9e0 recovered from eth_getBlockReceipts (receipt.contractAddress, direct deploy), creator 0xaa4273346d21a935bdf1302418d9531342d8142c. That creator is neither the attack-tx sender 0xdefc385d7038f391eb0063c2f7c238cfb55b206c nor the attack contract 0xb08ccb39741d746dd1818641900f182448eb5e41, so the victim is not attacker-deployed. Last change: over [15934352, 25345003] the victim emitted zero EIP-1967 Upgraded, zero BeaconUpgraded, zero Compound-fork NewImplementation(address,address), zero DiamondCut and zero AdminChanged events; its EIP-1967 implementation slot 0x3608...2bbc and beacon slot 0xa3f0...3d50 both read zero, so there is no implementation pointer to binary-search and the contract is a plain 8488-byte non-proxy vault. A full topic sweep of every log the vault ever emitted in that range returns only ERC20 Transfer (848x) plus a single OwnershipTransferred in the creation block, so deployment is the correct basis. Incident: attack tx in block 25345003, timestamp 1639849155 = 2021-12-18T17:39:15Z, status 1, 53 logs. Decoded from the receipt: a 937830 WFTM + 30 BTC flash loan from the Beethoven X vault 0x20dd72Ed959b6147912C2e529F0a0C651c33c9ce (fee 281.349 WFTM), the proceeds added as SpiritSwap BTC/WFTM LP 0x279b2c897737a50405ED2091694F225D83F2D3bA, then eight mint Transfers out of the vault to the attack contract (0.0324, 0.1147, 0.4065, 1.4406, 5.1049, 18.0894, 64.1009 and 227.1455 shares - the seven reentrant depositFor calls plus the final real LP deposit) and one burn of the 316.4350 total. The $30m loss is rekt.news' aggregate for the Grim vaults drained that day; this row anchors on the GrimBoostVault transaction rekt.news cites and DeFiHackLabs reproduces (src/test/2021-12/Grim_exp.sol, forked at block 25345002).

CErc20Delegator: `implementation` is storage slot 18 (slot 17 is `underlying` = 0xddafbb505ad214d7b80b1f830fccc89b60fb7a83). Slot 18 held 0xfcd8570ad81e6c77b8d252bebeba62ed980bd64d continuously over a 25-point probe of [15722098, 21120320] and the only NewImplementation(address,address) on the delegator is the 0x0 -> 0xfcd8570a write in its creation block. callTracer on the exploit tx confirms the delegator delegatecalls only that implementation, which itself has zero DELEGATECALL opcodes.

incident.name: HYPR L1StandardBridge uninitialized initialize()
incident.notes: The HYPR L1StandardBridge (an L1ChugSplashProxy) was deployed without being initialized, so the attacker called initialize() to set itself as the cross-domain messenger and then called finalizeERC20Withdrawal() to release 2.57M HYPR from the bridge.

sources.ref: onchain review: bridge proxy 0x40c31236b228935b0329eff066b1ad96e319595e created 2023-11-14T17:39:11Z by 0xb46c51ceaa6a191574f75dfcb4312e3c0b6405fb, unrelated to the attack sender; it is an L1ChugSplashProxy, which changes code through setCode/setStorage rather than an EIP-1967 Upgraded event, so nonStandardUpgradeArchitecture is set. The proxy's full pre-incident tx list contains only the deployment and user depositETH/depositERC20 calls (the two initialize() txs on it are dated 2023-12-14, after the incident), which at first suggested deployment as the last code change - superseded by the recheck below. Loss ~$200K per the PoC header; HYPR is the project's own token so no unit conversion applies. Recheck: reading the slot rather than the events shows the proxy had NO executing code at deployment - the EIP-1967 implementation slot was zero from the creation block 18571688 until block 18573592 (2023-11-15T00:02:47Z), where a binary search over eth_getStorageAt places the single write to 0xe468b43b4ae4d750cd6a5d7edacc1a751302c99c, the implementation the exploit delegatecalls (initialize() 0xc4d66de8 then finalizeERC20Withdrawal() 0xa9f9e675). The write came from the ProxyAdmin 0xba86cd28d937f1cc7c74a365368477408578364a and emitted only Initialized(2), no Upgraded event. Age measured from the implementation install, 6h24m after the proxy was deployed: 28.14 days rather than 28.41.

incident.documentedLastChange: 2023-11-15T00:02:47Z (block 18573592, tx 0x4cdfc7580172bee1a1decbe6190e0a018533259f324923c059f2833336cd0351): the bridge proxy's EIP-1967 implementation slot went 0x0 -> 0xe468b43b4ae4d750cd6a5d7edacc1a751302c99c, set through the ProxyAdmin 0xba86cd28d937f1cc7c74a365368477408578364a (selector 0x9623609d) by the deployer 0xb46c51ceaa6a191574f75dfcb4312e3c0b6405fb; the only log emitted was Initialized(2), no Upgraded event, which is why the event scan found none

The pool is a DelegateCallProxyManyToOne: its runtime hardcodes the implementation holder 0xffde4785e980a99fe10e6a87a67d243664b91b25 as an immutable and STATICCALLs it for the delegate target, so no EIP-1967 event is ever emitted and the deployment basis was wrong. Binary-searching eth_getStorageAt on slot 0 of that holder over [11398665, 13417949] shows the implementation moved twice after the pool was deployed: 0x71ed5fa0fde7b6dd8bc0dc25f7235d477e0faf77 -> 0x2483c55e414447cc78b0bfac77c1471d81baabdf at block 11800940 (2021-02-06T05:43:57Z) and -> 0x5bd628141c62a901e0a83e630ce5fafa95bbdee4 at block 12347624 (2021-05-01T10:07:22Z), then constant to the incident (61-point dense re-probe over [12347624, 13417949]). Corroborated by the proxy manager 0xd23dedc599bd56767e42d48484d6ca96ab01c115's own ManyToOne_ImplementationUpdated(bytes32,address) events for implementation id 0xe4105e36f4402bad908f77146a54b96b1aae362be2a9d940c0e19537431e1efb at exactly those two blocks, and by callTracer on the exploit tx, which shows the pool delegatecalling only 0x5bd628141c62a901e0a83e630ce5fafa95bbdee4 (a leaf: zero DELEGATECALL opcodes). Age 1634236663 - 1619863642 = 14,373,021 s (166.4 d), was 26,985,350 s (312.3 d) from deployment.

incident.name: Kinto K token clandestine proxy initialization
incident.lossOther: 790,148 USDC borrowed from Morpho Blue and never repaid + ~282.84 ETH taken out of the Uniswap v4/v3 K pools
incident.notes: The K token's UUPS/ERC-1967 proxy was deployed with its implementation slot left uninitialized in a separate transaction, so two seconds after creation an attacker wrote a clandestine implementation into the slot and masked it with a spoofed Upgraded event, and 113 days later that hidden implementation was used to write 1,000,000 K directly into the attacker's balance slot (no Transfer log, totalSupply untouched), which was dumped into the Uniswap v4/v3 pools and posted as Morpho Blue collateral to borrow USDC that was never repaid.

sources.ref: onchain review (Arbitrum). Victim: K token proxy 0x010700AB046Dd8e92b0e3587842080Df36364ed3 (Etherscan contract name UUPSProxy), created 2025-03-19T20:24:40Z block 317434592 by the Kinto deployer 0x660ad4b5a74130a4796b4d54bc6750ae93c86e6c in tx 0x35d5fc347c0ae0bd2cee08b2007455e118e89f297cc1faf8f5caf53808e3737a — neither the attacker nor the exploit-tx sender, so rule 2 holds. Exploit tx 0x579f0d9a... was sent by 0x905505e91cf4a929e9ff8a5544159195ba6e2ec3 through Multicall3 (0xca11bde05977b3631167028862be2a173976ca11) into attacker contract 0x0eb036e22ec6f795a9c2b85e07a1869af23e7bb4 and emitted zero logs; it wrote three K-token storage slots, of which 0xfc8bcaa1123599bcc5778aecceabd8c5757044f6c0ab074233eac11079e321e2 went 0 -> 0xd3c21bcecceda0000000 (999999999999999983222784 = ~1,000,000 K). balanceOf(0x6eb3731b52c8556073baa13d9e35d5a6713fc8ab) is 0 at block 356168983 and 999999999999999983222784 at block 356168984, that address never received a single K Transfer, and totalSupply is 1553019704644939833276904 at both blocks — an off-books mint by direct storage write. Implementation-slot (0x360894a1...) history recovered by binary-searching eth_getStorageAt, because only four Upgraded events exist and two of them are spoofed: creation 2025-03-19T20:24:40Z -> 0x1a16bcddd1bf92049e2a44e136081061eeace7c0; 2025-03-19T20:24:42Z block 317434602 tx 0xd17330df683adeec26a67ff6972a74ab60a1e5577c73d0e074d8e890fab5279c -> 0x7382bcbd6b361e218e1c1c3180201c2da6f3d210 (clandestine implementation) immediately followed in the same tx by an Upgraded event claiming 0x1a16bcdd... again; 2025-03-25T01:20:51Z block 319226261 the team emits Upgraded -> 0x96b7f2fa54a306bac6fde57f47f932a681dd9def but the slot is NOT changed and still reads 0x7382bcbd...; 2025-04-01T16:27:51Z block 321860388 slot -> 0x95fa23bb5e88ebc4a5fcf1210ccc526938e7dc58 with no event; 2025-04-08T18:15:22Z block 324296892 slot -> 0xe343c368c483da30a84d845eb3d2a209fbf6a683 with no event, and that is the executing code through the incident. Age is measured from 2025-04-08T18:15:22Z, the last actual change to the victim's executing code before the exploit (the exploit itself changed no code, only storage); the last team-emitted Upgraded event (2025-03-25T01:20:51Z, which would give 9,270,740 s) never reached the slot, and measuring from deployment as verify.mjs does would give 9,720,511 s. Loss: 791,182 USDC borrowed from Morpho Blue 0x6c247b1F6182318877311737BaC0844bAa518F5e by the attacker's ERC-4337 wallet 0xde86b457b2b5209bce1992434b82c7d54d3c2786 over 980 transfers with zero repayments, of which 790,148 USDC was forwarded to the attacker EOA; the EOA also received 566.14 ETH of internal transfers on 2025-07-10, of which 208.45 ETH (via 0x2ad5004c60...) and 74.85 ETH (via 1inch 0x1111111254421ca6dc452d289314280a0f8842a65) are the borrowed USDC swapped to ETH (581,696 and 208,452 USDC at the day's rate) and are therefore not double-counted, leaving ~282.84 ETH of genuine Uniswap pool proceeds. ETH/USD 2789.49 at the incident timestamp (curl https://coins.llama.fi/prices/historical/1752136391/coingecko:ethereum), giving 790,148 + 282.84*2789.49 = ~$1.579m, consistent with the ~$1.55m the team reported.

incident.notes: PropAMMWrapper paid out the integer returned by a USDC-denominated (6-decimal) quoter as raw units of tokenOut without asserting tokenOut was the quote token, so a WETH -> cbBTC route worth about 92 USDC transferred ~0.926 cbBTC (8 decimals) instead.

Deployment is exact; 486.6 days.

incident.name: LavaLending UniV3Wrapper unclaimed-fee inflation
incident.notes: UniV3Wrapper.getUnclaimedFees() ran its _limitFees() cap only against combined two-token fee growth, so fees generated in a single token by attacker-driven swaps in the USDC/USDC.e pool were added in full to getAssetsBasedOnPrice(), inflating the wrapper LP price read by the lending market's WrapperOracle and allowing an over-borrow.

incident.name: Level Finance
incident.notes: LevelReferralControllerV2: claimMultiple allowed repeated claims for the same epoch after an upgrade ~2 weeks earlier.

sources.ref: onchain review (RPC only, BSC): LevelReferralControllerV2 0x9f00fbd6c095d2c542687ed5afb68d9c3fb2f464 created 2023-04-17T14:20:34Z at block 27429090 (ts 1681741234). Immutability check rather than an upgrade scan: eth_getLogs for EIP-1967 Upgraded (topic 0xbc7cd75a20ee27fd9adebab32041f755214dbc6bffa90cc0225b39da2e5c2d3b) over [27429090, incident block 27828716] returns 0 logs; eth_getCode is byte-identical at the creation block and the incident block (9421 bytes both); and disassembling the runtime (skipping PUSH immediates) finds zero DELEGATECALL, CALLCODE, CREATE2 and SELFDESTRUCT opcodes, so the contract cannot execute foreign code and its own code provably never changed. There is therefore no non-standard upgrade channel to recover and the deployment basis is exact. The 'upgrade ~2 weeks earlier' in the notes is this deployment itself - V2 was a fresh contract replacing an earlier referral controller. CONFIRMED: codeAgeSeconds 1201166 (13.9d) unchanged.

onchain review: victim re-anchored from the LevelReferralControllerV2 implementation 0x9f00fbd6c095d2c542687ed5afb68d9c3fb2f464 to its TransparentUpgradeableProxy 0x977087422c008233615b572fbc3f209ed300063a, which emits 196 of the exploit tx's logs and whose EIP-1967 slot holds that implementation; the proxy was upgraded to the flawed implementation on 2023-04-18T08:16:11Z (block 27450541), one day after the implementation itself was deployed, so the executing code is 13.20 d old rather than the 13.90 d measured from implementation deployment. Creator 0x6442b001c5acce8cb71986ad65b22684821a927a is unrelated to attack sender 0x61bbd8c1bc09c4f4549f3f77be5ad61a9929412e

incident.name: LI.FI
incident.notes: LiFiDiamond: the GasZipFacet whose depositToGasZipERC20 performed an unvalidated arbitrary call was added by DiamondCut at 2024-07-16T10:03:23Z, about two hours (not five days) before the exploit; a further DiamondCut one minute later is the last change before the incident.

The selector 0x3d86ea87 (depositToGasZipERC20((address,address,address,address,uint256,bytes,bool),uint256,address)) appears in exactly one cut in the entire history: the Add of GasZipFacet 0xf28a352377663ca134bd27b582b1a9a4dad7e534 with selectors 0x3d86ea87, 0x867372e4 (depositToGasZipNative), 0xba956b9a, 0xb78e6e40, 0x3c36bac1 at block 20318349, 2024-07-16T10:03:23Z, tx 0xee96ca692ef8f6bdff087e0669d11950e71302896f3af5320b2504540f5d4f26. The exploit tx is 0xd82fe84e63b1aa52e1ce540582ee0895ba4a71ec5e7a632a3faa1aff3e763873, block 20318963, 2024-07-16T12:06:35Z (DeFiHackLabs src/test/2024-07/Lifiprotocol_exp.sol), i.e. 2h03m after the facet was installed. One further cut sits between them and is the last change before the incident: block 20318354, 2024-07-16T10:04:23Z, tx 0x802aa23c9689750b69ac1b7fbe237be880b61666cc2d90a800f9de22a2b77154, Replace of selectors 0x2541ec57/0xad673d88 to facet 0x376f99f7eade8a17f036fcff9eba978e66e5fd28. The cut before that pair was 2024-07-02T16:37:35Z (block 20220066); there is no DiamondCut at all on this diamond between 2024-07-02 and 2024-07-16, so the previously recorded 2024-07-11 facet-addition date is not an Ethereum-mainnet change. incident.name: Lodestar plvGLP exchange-rate manipulation
incident.notes: The lending market behaved as designed; Lodestar's plvGLP oracle derived the collateral price from the GlpDepositor's assets-per-share ratio, and the attacker inflated that ratio with GlpDepositor.donate() so a flash-loaned plvGLP position could borrow out the other Lodestar markets.

sources.ref: onchain review: lplvGLP market 0xcc25dac54a1a62061b596fd3baf7d454f34c56ff created 2022-11-21 by 0x67e57a0ec37768eaf99a364975ec4e1f98920d01 (Lodestar deployer), unrelated to attack sender 0xc29d94386ff784006ff8461c170d1953cc9e2b5c; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, so the market code was 18.9 days old; reported attacker profit ~$6.5M against ~$6.9M of protocol loss Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the victim is a Compound-fork CErc20Delegator, whose implementation lives in plain storage slot 18 rather than an EIP-1967 slot; binary-searching eth_getStorageAt on slot 18 over [40021576, 45121904] shows it holds 0x4eb611232ce3a738d9ee20467a5dd2ecf3b2d919 unchanged from creation to the incident (no NewImplementation in the window), the delegator runtime is byte-identical at both blocks, and the CToken implementation itself contains no DELEGATECALL, so the executing code dates from deployment.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim market 0xf8527dc5611b589cbb365acacaac0d1dc70b25cb created 2023-04-13T05:56:04Z by 0x27521eae4ee4153214cadc3ecd703b9b0326c908, unrelated to attack sender 0x4b92cc3452ef1e37528470495b86d3f976470734; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events on the market (it uses Compound's own NewImplementation instead - see the recheck below). The exploit transaction moved 274,358.98 BUSD and 1,077.93 WBNB through 0x85faac652b707fdf6907ef726751087f9e0b6687; lossUsd uses the ~$600K stated in the Midas post-mortem. Recheck (deployment basis was wrong, by a wide margin): the market is a Midas CErc20Delegator whose fallback delegatecalls `implementation` at storage slot 0 and, through the implementation's DiamondExtension fallback, a registered extension. Its own 618-byte runtime never changed (identical keccak(eth_getCode) at creation block 27304205 and incident block 29185769), but binary-searching eth_getStorageAt on slot 0 over [27304205, 29185768] finds six implementation swaps after deployment: 0x62473df8 (creation) -> 0x74517010 (block 27392990, 2023-04-16) -> 0x8e156d3c (27539708, 2023-04-21) -> 0xb8729ec6 (27543808, 2023-04-21) -> 0x13a2eb85 (28121136, 2023-05-11) -> 0x1d48efba (28886223, 2023-06-07) -> 0xf3c870b7c201515e2552d018ec2a15910fd35909 (29067669, 2023-06-13T14:21:12Z). The market's NewImplementation(address,address) log series matches the storage search block for block, and the diamond extension slot (extensions[0] at keccak(keccak("diamond.standard.diamond.storage")+2)) was rewritten to 0xe4fea88df81eba4f579208fa5abeb10aaf84e3f4 in that same block 29067669. Both addresses are exactly the two the victim delegatecalls in the exploit trace. The exploited exchange-rate code was therefore 4.1 days old, not the 65.5 days the deployment basis gave.

incident.name: NORMIE swapAndLiquify triggered on the token's own balance
incident.notes: NORMIE's _transfer fired an internal swapAndLiquify of the contract's accumulated fee balance whenever that balance crossed a threshold randomised from block.timestamp and block.difficulty, with no slippage bound, so flash-swapped NORMIE routed through the SushiSwap pair let the attacker choose when the contract sold and capture the proceeds.

sources.ref: onchain review: NORMIE 0x7F12d13B34F5F4f0a9449c16Bcd42f0da47AF200 created 2024-03-06T22:10:17Z by 0xd8056b0f8aa2126a8db6f0b3109fe9127617beb2, not the attack-tx sender 0xf7f3a556ac21d081f6dba961b6a84e52e37a717d; no EIP-1967 events, 80.2 days old. Its verified source shows _transfer computing tokensToSwap from _minimumTokensBeforeSwap scaled by (keccak256(block.timestamp, block.difficulty) % 11) + 90 and comparing it with balanceOf(address(this)), i.e. a self-balance-triggered swapback. Loss $490K per the DeFiHackLabs 2024 index entry and the PoC header.

incident.name: NXUSD Cauldron oracle manipulation
incident.notes: The NXUSD CauldronV2 market valued its Curve LP collateral from the pool's live state, so an Aave flash loan that imbalanced the two Curve pools let the attacker borrow far more NXUSD than the deposited collateral was worth.

sources.ref: onchain review: CauldronV2 0xC0A7a7F141b6A5Bce3EC1B81823c8AFA456B6930 created 2022-09-05T10:20:47Z by 0x6b4020dc274283afc240feccc27eff3a1f0f44f4, not the attack-tx sender 0x69992a2e5d6ec031ab16733975110f0b43a0b1af; no EIP-1967 events, so the executing code was 1.38 days old.
