incident.name: Ocean BPool asymmetric single-sided join/exit with SideStaking
incident.notes: Ocean's BPool join and exit maths are asymmetric for maximum single-sided deposits and SideStaking mirrored each join and exit with automatic datatoken staking, so repeatedly joining flash-swapped mOCEAN single-sided and exiting the BPT returned more mOCEAN than went in.

sources.ref: onchain review: the BPool logic contract 0xBB3051dF2D3E408DAE6E6dAa2296BC6215F0dCFd (the address the PoC header names as the vulnerable BPool code; the eight drained pools are clones of it) was created 2022-05-26T15:32:12Z by 0xc7ec1970b09224b317c52d92f37f5e1e4ff6b687, not the attack-tx sender 0x3fa8cf7fea68c8e76a9838d77889464ddfb6a6cf; no EIP-1967 events, 1490.6 days old. SideStaking 0x3EFDD8f728c8e774aB81D14d0B2F07a8238960f4 supplies the mirrored datatoken side. Loss stated in the project's own mOCEAN token, so no USD figure is asserted; ~127.86K mOCEAN is far above the $1,000 floor at any mOCEAN price traded around that date.

incident.name: ODOS

incident.name: OMPxContract treasury-inventory mispricing
incident.notes: getBuyBackPrice divides the contract's ETH reserve by token.totalSupply() even though the contract itself held ~79% of that supply as unsold inventory, so purchase() sold that inventory for a fraction of the reserve share it entitles the buyer to and buyBack() immediately redeemed it at the full per-supply price, letting a flash-loaned purchase/buyBack loop drain the reserve.

sources.ref: onchain review: OMPxContract 0x09a80172ed7335660327cd664876b5df6fe06108 was created 2018-04-10T18:22:23Z at block 5417094 by 0xeb79db7b4ce44bfb549104cafc8f51cc93a686fb, unrelated to attack sender 0x40d115198d71cab59668b51dd112a07d273d5831 or its attack contract 0xfaddf57d079b01e53d1fe3476cc83e9bcc705854. Mechanism confirmed against state at block 20468779: OMPX totalSupply 2,269,323e18 with 1,799,614e18 (79.3%) held by the victim itself, ETH reserve 5.6955 ETH, and the discount coefficients read from discounts(i) are 198/190/180/150 against descPrecision 100, i.e. purchase is nominally at a 1.5-2x markup - the profit comes from the totalSupply denominator, not from a discount. The trace shows 7 purchase/buyBack rounds: round one pays 100 ETH with 93.2257 ETH refunded (net 6.7743 ETH) and is bought back for 9.2914 ETH. Loss not recorded in USD: the victim's ETH balance fell from 5.695503 to 1.322633 ETH, i.e. 4.372870 ETH, matching the 4.37 ETH in the DeFiHackLabs PoC; the ~$107k headline circulated elsewhere is irreconcilable with that (the PoC itself quotes ~$11.5k). Order-of-magnitude sanity check only (ETH ~ $2,400 in Aug 2024, so ~$10k): above the $1,000 floor.
loss converted at the incident timestamp (1722938291) via DefiLlama coins: 4.37 ETH x $2,465.70 = $10,775

incident.name: OpBorrowing liquidation clears shared LToken debt
incident.notes: OpBorrowing.liquidate() settled positions through LToken.repayBorrowEndByOpenLev(), which zeroes the borrower's entire LToken debt shared with OpenLevV1 margin trades, so the attacker reentered OpBorrowing.borrow() from the untrusted dexData swap callback of marginTrade() to open a dust position, liquidated it, and then withdrew the now debt-free margin collateral with payoffTrade().

sources.ref: onchain review: victim 0xf436f8fe7b26d87eb74e5446acec2e8ad4075e47 is the OPBorrowingDelegator created 2023-03-22 by 0xe9547cf7e592f83c5141bb50648317e35d27d29b (OpenLeverage deployer), not by attack sender 0x5bb5b6d41c3e5e41d9b9ed33d12f1537a1293d5f; it is a custom delegator that emits NewImplementation rather than EIP-1967 Upgraded, and its only NewImplementation event (block 37968060, 2024-04-18) is the post-incident patch, so the exploited code dates from the constructor-set implementation

incident.name: Poolz LockedDeal CreateMassPools integer overflow
incident.notes: LockedDeal's CreateMassPools() sums the per-pool amounts in an unchecked uint256 addition, so an overflowing amount array let the attacker register pools crediting the contract's whole MNZ/SIP/ECIO/WOD balance while transferring almost nothing in.

sources.ref: onchain review: LockedDeal 0x8BfAA473a899439d8E07BF86a8C6cE5De42fE54B created 2021-07-29T11:05:08Z by 0xf7f1f00b13f4c3d818f052498902067ab91a3a66, unrelated to attack sender 0x190cd736f5825ff0ae0141b5c9cb7fcd042cef2a; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, age measured from deployment. The realised proceeds came from selling the released project tokens over subsequent transactions, so lossUsd uses the ~$390K reported by PeckShield across BSC, Ethereum and Polygon deployments.

incident.name: Popsicle
incident.notes: Fee rewards (token0/1PerSharePaid) not updated on LP token transfer, letting multiple holders claim same fees.

incident.name: PredyFinance
incident.notes: attacker-registered pair with malicious priceFeed and take/supply bypassed solvency checks to withdraw pool

sources.ref: Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): PredyPool sets no EIP-1967 implementation or beacon slot and its runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 204572377 and the incident block 211107442; its ten DELEGATECALL sites are all solc external-library calls whose target is a PUSH20 constant baked into the runtime (0x0493a63109f37f08376fd0c321b012c34f946ca7, 0x2140f617e8cedb9e7f1b4f2c3f79cd064c7c088a, 0x2d756f7912b5c61f35ca3e5b310c7c133a90977c, 0x5e8d28bd2abe77e9d3e9dd8ccc1727eda616ace0, 0xde12aa19734dacbd34cedde14f8290a70a85537f, 0xe64ccc2549ed5e51417f30cc57b0830759a30e25), each deployed in the same batch by the same deployer 0x4f071924d66bbc71a5254217893cc7d49938b1c4 within 170 blocks of the pool and byte-identical over the window, so the library set cannot be repointed and deployment is exact.

onchain review: victim re-anchored from implementation 0x7b8b944ab2f24c829504a7a6d70fce5298f2147c to the proxy the protocol runs at, 0x9215748657319b17fecb2b5d086a3147bfbc8613, which holds that implementation in its EIP-1967 slot and emits the exploit transaction's logs while the implementation emits none; age measured from when the proxy started running the implementation rather than from the implementation's own deployment (1650036s -> 1650032s)

incident.name: PresaleV5 slot0 pricing manipulation
incident.notes: PresaleV5.buyWithEth() priced the sale token from the current slot0 of a Uniswap V3 pool with no TWAP or independent check, so a flash-loaned sale into that pool let the attacker buy presale tokens at a manipulated discount and sell them straight back, repeated within one transaction.

sources.ref: onchain review: presale proxy 0x9a15bb3A8feC8d0d810691BafE36F6e5D42360f7 created 2024-10-09T13:42:11Z by 0x26c6b1cd843c8e5aa1c9958df95d85424d390928, not the attack-tx sender 0x3a7e13dacccd3de56b8186987f348bfd21dc4ec5; six EIP-1967 Upgraded events, the last at block 21994149 on 2025-03-07T09:36:47Z installing 0x09c135aacd4a82b08890e930dfdc3143b4578d45 (the implementation the PoC names), so the executing code was 164.8 days old. 2.3157 ETH x $4,209.45 at the incident timestamp (DefiLlama) = $9,748.

incident.name: Prisma Finance
incident.notes: MigrateTroveZap: onFlashLoan did not validate initiator/params, letting anyone migrate (and re-open with attacker params) other users' troves.

sources.ref: onchain review (no exploit tx in this row; DeFiHackLabs src/test/2024-03/Prisma_exp.sol names the vulnerable contract and the attack tx 0x00c503b595946bccaea3d58025b5f9b3726177bbdc9674e634244135282116c7. Incident block located by binary-searching eth_getBlockByNumber to measurement.incidentTimestamp -> ethereum block 19532470, 2024-03-28T12:00:00Z). VICTIM CORRECTED: this row previously pointed at 0xB8FA880840A64c25318989B907cCb58FD7A324Df, which is not the MigrateTroveZap described in the notes but a Prisma ConvexDepositToken - an EIP-1167 clone whose 45-byte runtime hardcodes the ConvexDepositToken master 0x838a35e3a63df3cd27d321f87980f17f51218fa1 (both verified under that name). The MigrateTroveZap is 0xcC7218100da61441905e0c327749972e3cBeE9EE (Etherscan-verified as `MigrateTroveZap`), created 2024-03-20T08:30:35Z at block 19474738 by tx 0xc8d4059c4394812b142dc88a8a8534687bb8857c10f2093bffc9c44a90ee6f56 from 0xd8531a94100f15af7521a7b6e724ac4959e0a025 (a Prisma deployer, also the deployer of the ConvexDepositToken master; not the attacker). The zap is immutable: zero DELEGATECALL opcodes in its runtime, no EIP-1967 Upgraded event, and byte-identical eth_getCode at the creation block and the incident block, so the deployment basis is exact. Code age falls from 122.0 days (measured against the wrong contract) to 703765s, ~8.1 days - the unvalidated onFlashLoan shipped eight days before it was exploited.
merged with the duplicate prisma record, adopting its exploit tx and exact block-timestamp measurement

incident.name: Pro Token
incident.notes: The player proxy's public exec path lacked a per-call entitlement or one-shot guard, allowing 305 fixed-size Pro-to-USDT reward swaps to rotating attacker-controlled winners in one transaction.

incident.name: Projekt Reward Vault
incident.notes: Permissionless trackPurchase credited ETH allocations from a buyer's token-balance delta without verifying that the buyer had spent ETH or made a genuine purchase, enabling fabricated allocations to be withdrawn.

incident.name: proxy_b7e1
incident.notes: Crafted calldata to order function (selector 0x9b3e9b92) with negative/underflow-style order params drains the proxy's entire USDT balance.

incident.name: PRXVTStaking reward accounting not settled on transfer
incident.notes: PRXVTStaking issued transferable stPRXVT receipts but never settled or reset reward accounting on transfer, so moving the staked balance through a series of fresh CREATE2 addresses let each one report the full accumulated earned() and call claimReward() again.

sources.ref: onchain review: PRXVTStaking (verified source) created 2025-12-31 by 0xa116959ffe4f64b82e294ef2209b34423c078e9f (not the attacker 0x7407f9bd...), no Upgraded events - the exploited code was under 8 hours old. The PoC loop deploys Attack2 helpers with CREATE2, transfers stPRXVT to each and calls claimReward(). Loss 32.8 ETH; DefiLlama records $97,000 (Staking Logic Flaw, Base).

incident.name: Pump
incident.notes: Template token's buyToken pricing lets an attacker buy tokens far too cheaply after seeding LP, then dump them for profit.

incident.name: Punk Protocol pool re-initialization
incident.notes: The Punk pool's initialize() carried neither access control nor an initialized guard, so the attacker re-initialized it with their own forge_ address and then called withdrawToForge() to sweep the pooled stablecoins.

sources.ref: onchain review: the single attack tx touches all three sibling pools - Punk USDC 0x3bc6aa2d (used here as victim), Punk USDT 0x1f3b04c8c96a31c7920372ffa95371c80a4bfb0d and Punk DAI 0x929cb86046e421abf7e1e02de7836742654d49d6 - which share the same flawed code; 0x3bc6aa2d created 2021-08-02 by 0xe36cc0432619247ab12f1cdd19bb3e7a24a7f47c, not by attack sender 0x1d5a5640. lossUsd 8,950,000 is the protocol-wide figure (rekt); ~$4.95m was later returned

incident.name: Pythia staking reward re-claim
incident.notes: claimRewards() paid out against the caller's current staking-token balance without settling or resetting reward accounting when that balance was transferred, so the attacker recycled the same stake through fresh helper contracts and claimed the reward pool ~30 times in one transaction.

sources.ref: onchain review: staking contract 0xe2910b29... created by 0xae730f689ac162440536ce006caff10fe759ab52 on 2024-09-02T17:31:59Z, 10 hours before the attack; attack sender 0xd861e6f1... is unrelated to the creator

incident.name: Qixi token transfer underflow
incident.notes: The QIXI token's unchecked fee arithmetic in transfer() underflows the liquidity pair's balance, letting the attacker inflate their own holding and swap it for the pair's WBNB.

incident.name: Qubit Finance (QBridge)
incident.notes: Ethereum-side QBridge: deposit path allowed a 0-value deposit (safeTransferFrom on address(0) token) to emit a Deposit event minting unbacked qXETH collateral on BSC. Sources: halborn analysis; flaw located in QBridgeHandler on Ethereum.

incident.name: Quixotic marketplace unvalidated ERC-20 transfer path
incident.notes: The Quixotic NFT marketplace let an order specify the ERC-20 to pull and the account to pull it from without proving the order came from that account, so every wallet holding an allowance to the marketplace could be drained of OP and other tokens.

sources.ref: onchain review: the PoC carries no transaction hash, so transactions touching the marketplace 0x065e8A87b8F11aED6fAcf9447aBe5E8C5D7502b6 in the PoC's fork block window (13591381-13591390) were listed with eth_getLogs; the one recorded here, 0x5dc51972...92e6 at block 13591384, was sent by 0x0a0805082ea0fc8bfdcc6218a986efda6704efe5, the address the PoC pranks as the exploiter, and three sibling transactions in the same window repeat the drain. The marketplace was created 2022-05-25T20:21:59Z by 0xec1557a67d4980c948cd473075293204f4d280fd, not the attacker; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, 36.4 days old. Loss $100K per the DeFiHackLabs 2022 index entry for this PoC.

incident.name: Rabby Wallet SwapRouter arbitrary call
incident.notes: Rabby's swap router forwarded an unvalidated (target, calldata) pair from the caller, so the attacker made the router call transferFrom on token contracts and sweep balances from every user who had approved it.

sources.ref: onchain review: router 0x6eb211caf6d304a76efe37d9abdfaddc2d4363d1 created 2022-09-12T01:35:55Z by 0x5853ed4f26a3fcea565b3fbc698bb19cdf6deb85, unrelated to the attack sender; unverified, no EIP-1967 events, age from deployment. incident.name: Radiant Capital (flashloan rounding)
incident.notes: LendingPool proxy: the newly activated native USDC reserve was exploited ~6-9 seconds after activation (2024-01-02 18:53:29 UTC) via the known Aave-v2 fresh-market index rounding window. Extreme young-code case; last change = reserve activation (quillaudits analysis), not a proxy upgrade.

incident.name: Radiant Capital (multisig malware)
incident.notes: 3 signer devices compromised with malware signing a malicious transferOwnership; contracts then upgraded by the attacker. Key compromise.

incident.name: RADT DAO wrap withdraw arbitrary transfer
incident.notes: The RADT wrapper's withdraw(address,address,uint256) let any caller move RADT out of an arbitrary account, so the attacker stripped the RADT/USDT pair, synced it and sold RADT into the drained reserves.

sources.ref: onchain review: wrapper 0x01112eA0679110cbc0ddeA567b51ec36825aeF9b created 2022-08-19T14:09:34Z by 0xffa253745772f1c3b659583cd47a9858286b8e61, unrelated to attack sender 0xa957910cb426cb52dfc6dff5e582860a22db70d2; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events (this proxy emits none - see the recheck below). Loss verified onchain: 94,304.58 USDT left the RADT/USDT pair 0xaF8fb60f310DCd8E488e4fa10C48907B7abf115e to the attack contract. Recheck (deployment basis was wrong): the wrapper's runtime is a 98-byte proxy that SLOADs 0x360894a13ba1a3210667c828492db98dca3e2076cc3735a920a3ca505d382bbb - the raw keccak("eip1967.proxy.implementation"), one less than the standard EIP-1967 slot - and delegatecalls it, which is why an EIP-1967 event/slot scan sees nothing. Reading that slot instead: it held 0xe0d971450997bef4508abeae8082291c2658f2b8 at the creation block 20579790 and 0x9122191d7b2ccf11a2600de4eafd6b8cd3d03a62 at the incident block; a binary search over [20579790, 21572418] puts the single change at block 20627998 (2022-08-21T06:21:16Z), written silently by the deployer, with no Upgraded log anywhere on the proxy. 0x9122191d7b2ccf11a2600de4eafd6b8cd3d03a62 is the address the victim delegatecalls in the exploit (selector d9caed12, the withdraw path). Age measured from that swap: 32.9 days rather than 34.6.

incident.documentedLastChange: 2022-08-21T06:21:16Z (BSC block 20627998, tx 0x028d710cfbd0c034c39c0d698e024784a155446b20f01c4b10c72a3a8ef36a6b sent by the deployer 0xffa253745772f1c3b659583cd47a9858286b8e61): the proxy's implementation slot 0x360894a13ba1a3210667c828492db98dca3e2076cc3735a920a3ca505d382bbb changed 0xe0d971450997bef4508abeae8082291c2658f2b8 -> 0x9122191d7b2ccf11a2600de4eafd6b8cd3d03a62 with no event emitted; found by binary-searching eth_getStorageAt on that slot

incident.name: RANT pays out BNB for tokens sent to the token contract
incident.notes: A flash-loan-funded buy of 9.66e25 RANT from the RANT/WBNB pair followed by a single transfer of 1.07e25 RANT into the RANT token contract returned enough BNB to repay the loan and keep 311 BNB, i.e. RANT's transfer handler redeems tokens sent to itself out of its own reserves at a rate detached from the pool price.

incident.name: Rari Fuse (Pool reentrancy)
incident.notes: Fuse pool cEther (fToken) exitMarket/borrow cross-function reentrancy via .call value transfer before state update.

sources.ref: onchain review (no exploit tx in this row; DeFiHackLabs src/test/2022-04/Rari_exp.sol names the same victim as fETH-127. Incident block located by binary-searching eth_getBlockByNumber to measurement.incidentTimestamp -> ethereum block 14685453, 2022-04-30T12:00:00Z). The victim 0x26267e41CeCa7C8E0f143554Af707336f27Fa051 is a Fuse CEtherDelegator (verified) created at block 13673508, 2021-11-23T22:34:04Z. It emits no EIP-1967 Upgraded event; its fallback reads the implementation from storage slot 0 (it delegatecalls sload(0) with selector 0x1db78944 = `_prepare()`, Fuse's auto-upgrade hook, then delegatecalls sload(0) with the original calldata), and `implementation()` (0x5c60da1b) returns that same slot. Two independent checks show the pointer never moved: eth_getLogs for Compound's NewImplementation(address,address) over [creation, incident] returns exactly one event, the 0x0 -> 0xd77e28a1b9a9cfe1fc2eee70e391c05d25853cbf write in the creation block, and a binary search of eth_getStorageAt on slot 0 finds it unchanged since creation. The implementation 0xd77e28a1b9a9cfe1fc2eee70e391c05d25853cbf (deployed 2021-10-01T07:05:21Z) itself contains zero DELEGATECALL opcodes, so it is a leaf. Fuse's `_prepare()` auto-upgrade never fired for this market and the deployment basis is exact.

re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis (independent re-check of the existing note). Slot 0 held 0xd77e28a1b9a9cfe1fc2eee70e391c05d25853cbf at all 25 sample points across [13673508, 14685453], and the only NewImplementation(address,address) event on the delegator is the 0x0 -> 0xd77e28a1 write in its creation block 13673508.

exploit tx backfilled and verified onchain (block 14684814): the exit-fee reentrancy drain of Fuse pool 127 fETH 0x26267e41ceca7c8e0f143554af707336f27fa051 (this row's victim), the tx DeFiHackLabs reproduces and CertiK's analysis cites; the wider incident drained ~7 pools across sequential txs from the same attacker

incident.notes: The Reaper vault exposed a deposit path that took the source address as a parameter with no check that it was the caller, so anyone could pull tokens from every wallet that had approved the vault.

Creation resolved by binary search over eth_getCode to block 41839240, 2022-07-02T12:48:36Z, creator 0x6539519e69343535a2af6583d9bae3ad74c6a293, not the attack-tx sender 0x5636e55e4a72299a0f194c001841e2ce75bb527a; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, 30.7 days old. incident.name: ResupplyFi
incident.notes: empty-market share-price inflation (crvUSD donation + 1-wei mint) triggers precision/rounding in ResupplyPair's exchange rate, enabling a 10M reUSD borrow.

incident.name: Revamp contributor reward cap self-triggered
incident.notes: revamp() rewards earlier contributors from later contributions with only a 2x cap and no check that the two contributions are independent, so the attacker sized a first contribution to half the contract's balance, funded a second from a helper address and withdrew both principals plus the capped reward.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim 0x46280c1a2e17cfc151f50a885363408368bb163a created 2025-07-06T14:05:02Z by 0x6915ffc19ca9019608dcf4a912504b795e643823, which is not the attack-tx sender 0x42579d63bd5945fcfde5adff4edc40c34869914e; 0 EIP-1967 Upgraded events on the victim before the incident; code age measured from deployment (onchain). 2.99 BNB x $650.702246/BNB at the incident timestamp 1773889032 (DefiLlama coingecko:binancecoin) = $1,946.

incident.notes: V3Utils executed a caller-supplied swap target and calldata without validating it, so the attacker made the helper call transferFrom on tokens and pull balances from users who had approved it.

incident.notes: RFB derives its reward lottery from on-chain values a contract can read in the same transaction (block data and balances), so the attacker predicted the outcome and only entered when it paid out.

sources.ref: onchain review: RFB 0x26f1457f067bF26881F311833391b52cA871a4b5 created 2022-12-03T15:45:54Z by 0x5c0a527beef80f5e479abb0776e53073aaa2a935, unrelated to attack sender 0x5f7db41e2196080f397cdcf8dd58e8adfdaf2ade; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, age measured from deployment. lossUsd converts the 12 BNB reported by DeFiHackLabs: 12 BNB x $289.90 at incidentTimestamp 1670260745 (DefiLlama coingecko:binancecoin) = $3,479.

incident.name: Rho Markets PriceOracleV2 ETH feed overwrite
incident.notes: PriceOracleV2 keys chainlinkPriceFeeds by getUnderlying(rToken) = configs[rToken].underlying, so listing a Rho WBTC market whose RTokenConfig was never set (underlying defaulting to address(0)) made setChainlinkPriceFeed write the WBTC/USD aggregator over the entry shared with the native-ETH market Rho ETH, whose getUnderlyingPrice then returned $63,653.14 per ETH and let the attacker borrow 942.71 wstETH against 84.14 ETH of collateral.

sources.ref: Onchain review over plain JSON-RPC. Etherscan v2 does not serve Scroll (chainid 534352 is rejected as unsupported), so the victim's creation was resolved with no explorer, by binary-searching eth_getCode against the l2beat Scroll archive endpoint used as RPC_URL_SCROLL (SCROLL_RPC_URL, https://rpc.l2beat.com/scroll/...): PriceOracleV2 proxy 0x653c2d3a1e4ac5330de3c9927bb9bdc51008f9d5 first has code at block 6812594 (deployTimestamp 1719141379 = 2024-06-23T11:16:19Z), creation tx 0x06aa1fb0989cb874d876c0b276d972807fcf72f0ba6430cbe32eded26bd4e928 recovered from eth_getBlockReceipts (direct deploy), creator 0xaa6745049b1a7f9f63524aef23db924e2e45d221 - neither the attack-tx sender 0xe000008459b74a91e306a47c808061dfa372000e nor its attack contract 0xe2704980704b26f9ee909daa44750498bc8c3702, so the victim is not attacker-deployed. Last change: over [6812594, 7580143] the victim emitted exactly one EIP-1967 Upgraded event and one AdminChanged, both in the creation block 6812594 itself (the ERC1967 proxy constructor), and zero BeaconUpgraded, zero Compound-fork NewImplementation(address,address) and zero DiamondCut; a binary search of eth_getStorageAt on the EIP-1967 implementation slot 0x3608...2bbc over [6812594, 7580143] shows it holds 0xb14df613f4b30ffffe9811a11f2931de011391d9 unchanged from creation through the incident, so the code never changed after deployment and deployment is the basis (upgradeEventCount 1 is the raw log count and coincides with deployment). The implementation's verified source names the contract PriceOracleV2. Root cause reconstructed onchain: the oracle was bound to the Rho comptroller 0x8a67ab98a291d1aea2e1eb0a79ae4ab7f2d76041 by NewPriceOracle at blocks 6812595/6812596. At block 7580111 (2024-07-19T08:58:32Z) the Rho admin EOA 0x83e987c3fd6b4e43a8514e69b71ea09ff0ac4716 listed a new Rho WBTC market 0x1d73ead2bbea318344fccd7142f70488bab08f44 and called setChainlinkPriceFeed(rWBTC, 0x61C432B58A43516899d8dF33A5F57edb8d57EB77) in tx 0x9d2388a0c449c6265b968d86f0f54e75a5b82e2b04176e35eefdff5f135547ec, without ever calling setRTokenConfig for rWBTC - so configs[rWBTC].underlying read address(0), the same key already used by the native-ETH market Rho ETH 0x639355f34ca9935e0004e30bd77b9ce2ada0e692 (configs[rETH] = {underlying: address(0), decimals: 18}). chainlinkPriceFeeds[address(0)] therefore flipped from 0x6bF14CB0A831078629D993FDeBcB182b21A8774C ('ETH / USD') to 0x61C432B58A43516899d8dF33A5F57edb8d57EB77 ('WBTC / USD', 8 decimals, latestRoundData answer 6365314400000), and getUnderlyingPrice(rETH) went from 3384.18e18 at block 7580110 to 63653.144e18 at block 7580111, returning to 3401.14e18 at block 7580675 (09:14:10Z) when the admin re-pointed the ETH market at the ETH/USD feed in tx 0x30879b0dbee84ba41aa1fc6ef71e81a8985bf8509796ca45f30ec4640b338db4 - a 564-block, 938-second window of mispricing. The attack tx sits 32 blocks / 77 seconds into it, at block 7580143, timestamp 1721379589 = 2024-07-19T08:59:49Z, status 1, 23 logs: flash-loan 84.1390 WETH from 0x97a90e651b0a5cf76484513469249d9bffe4c73b, unwrap to native ETH, mint 83.8673 rETH, enter seven markets, borrow 942.7091 wstETH from rwstETH 0xe4fc4c444effb5eca80274c021f652980794eae6, swap it for 1103.6836 WETH on 0x05dff4a55473562dd26bdbe4f74410a7307175bf and unwrap 1019.5026 WETH after repaying the loan; seven further borrow transactions repeated it before the fix. Category judgement: no attacker transaction moved any price - the wrong price was already sitting in the victim's own storage, written by the protocol's own admin - so this is a configuration error in the victim (code-bug per CONTRIBUTING) and not oracle-manipulation, notwithstanding DefiLlama's 'Oracle Manipulation / Spot Price Manipulation' label. lossUsd 7600000 is DefiLlama's incident total (api.llama.fi/hacks, defillamaId 4808); the funds were subsequently returned, which does not affect the measurement. Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): re-read the EIP-1967 implementation slot 0x3608...2bbc directly rather than trusting events - it holds 0xb14df613f4b30ffffe9811a11f2931de011391d9 at the incident block 7580143 and at the creation block 6812594, with a binary search of eth_getStorageAt over that range finding no intermediate write; the proxy runtime is byte-identical at both blocks and the implementation 0xb14df613f4b30ffffe9811a11f2931de011391d9 contains no DELEGATECALL of its own, so the executing code cannot have changed after deployment.

sources.ref: onchain review: oracle 0x16f3ae9c1727ee38c98417ca08ba785bb7641b5b created 2022-11-14 by 0xc5fc2cbf32c09f89f91caf2023884729116ea5d1 (Sentiment deployer), unrelated to attack sender 0xdd0cdb4c3b887bc533957bc32463977e432e49c3; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, so the code was ~141 days old; classified oracle-manipulation per the dataset precedent that price-skewing (read-only) reentrancy is an oracle failure rather than a state-changing code bug

incident.name: Shoebill BTC market oracle misconfiguration
incident.notes: The price oracle the Shoebill comptroller reads was upgraded to integrate solvBTC and solvBTC.BBN and returned a grossly overstated price for the sb Solv BTC market, so 0.005 sbSolvBTC of collateral supported borrowing 19.51 WBTC and 1.597 tBTC - a defect in the victim's freshly deployed oracle code and its onchain feed configuration, not manipulation of a market price by the attacker.

sources.ref: onchain review on BOB (chainid 60808, 0xed88; Etherscan does not serve it, but https://rpc.gobob.xyz answers eth_getCode, eth_getStorageAt and eth_getLogs at historical blocks and https://explorer.gobob.xyz/api/v2 resolves names and creators). The exploit transaction at block 8751267 enters two markets on Unitroller 0xb7ed6c062caaacb1a13f317e0a751289280fc306 and emits two Compound Borrow events: 19.51269875 WBTC from sb Wrapped BTC 0x5c46d274ed8abcae2964b63c0360ad3ccc384daa and 1.5973028815 tBTC from sb tBTC v2 0x2925df9eb2092b53b06a06353a7249af3a8b139e, against getAssetsIn collateral of only 500029 units (0.00500029) of sb Solv BTC 0x0f1f734c1d69774be2c1a8eba3d1a43f4576faf7. The comptroller's oracle() at the incident block is 0xE103F874B2D144C5B327FA3d57069Bb19c0779e2, recorded here as the victim because it is the contract holding the mispricing; it is an EIP-1967 TransparentUpgradeableProxy created 2024-05-01T09:47:33Z at block 847433 by 0xcFf0E961d0DEC9dadF8587F66f158738e1366264 (Shoebill deployer), unrelated to attack sender 0x58491274790b6dfc9233b09d8212e1957cc37a03 or its attack contract 0x06ca861fc14a58a4fd5fdda45e904304785ae238. A full eth_getLogs scan of the Upgraded topic over blocks 847433-8751267 returns exactly two events: the creation-block install of 0x037d45ca2b024a25a6091212761e0757227b60c8 and a replacement with 0x8a34c9ada41318e6d4b8652ca6349540ec5eb772 at block 8747068, 2024-10-31T06:28:43Z, in tx 0x490b9b66d79e6a1282711cc20d0e8faf903bcb971f2bc5c1f0a4b789468f036e sent by the same Shoebill deployer - 2 hours 20 minutes (8,398 s) before the exploit, and still the live implementation today. That upgrade is the solvBTC/solvBTC.BBN integration the post-mortem blames. Classified code-bug rather than oracle-manipulation: no market price was moved by the attacker, the oracle's own deployed code and configuration returned the wrong value. Loss not recorded in USD: the amounts are the two Borrow event values, matching the 19.512 wBTC and 1.597 tBTC the post-mortem reports the attacker bridged out; the $1.52m headline from SlowMist and Shoebill's own announcement is consistent as an order-of-magnitude sanity check (BTC ~ $72k on 2024-10-31) and is far above the $1,000 floor, but is not recorded as a high-confidence figure.
loss converted at the incident timestamp (1730364521) via DefiLlama coins: 19.51 WBTC x $72,037.00 + 1.597 tBTC x $71,884.00 = $1,520,241

incident.name: SingularityDynaVault
incident.notes: dynBaseUSDCv3 oracle path (Uni V3 fee tier 42 / zero-liquidity fallbacks) made totalAssets() count only idle USDC, so a flashloan deposit minted inflated shares redeemable for the real reserves.

sources.ref: Onchain review: dynBaseUSDCv3 0x67b93f6676bd1911c5fae7ffa90fff5f35e14dcd created 2026-01-17T12:21:51Z (Base block 40932782) by 0xcd231d4ba7b15a4722ac057419d9cd7689e7b8db, not the attack-tx sender 0x5c2cbe53f2ce1b58532d4985a9b9d3db87d3af4c. The vault's 45-byte runtime is an EIP-1167 minimal proxy (363d3d373d3d3d363d73) whose master 0xea7975c2fec1ae9e3058bb5f99d8e26dbc816811 is baked into the bytecode and cannot be repointed; the master's own delegatecall targets 0x3ce426bb2fcb9e1300bbe03e2d34d7b3b7347db5 and 0x4c3df500989df0f6670b99018811b94d591cc5a0 - the other two addresses executed in the victim's context in the exploit trace - are PUSH20 link-time constants in the master's bytecode. keccak(eth_getCode) on the clone is identical at the creation and incident blocks and no EIP-1967 or beacon slot is set, so the deployment basis is exact.

incident.notes: SocketGateway: the swap route registered 3 days earlier (routeId 406 -> 0xCC5fDA5e3cA925bd0bb428C8b2669496eE43067e) performed an unvalidated user-controlled call, draining approvals. Route installation emits NewRouteAdded(uint32,address), not an EIP-1967 Upgraded event.

The previously recorded day-level date 2024-01-12 is one day early; age 345600s -> 279373s. The registry row socketgateway.json measures the same change against the exact exploit-tx timestamp 1705432283 and therefore reports 305256s.

incident.name: Sodium session-key validation bypass
incident.notes: Sodium's executeWithSodiumAuthSession signature path accepted an attacker-chosen session key with no owner authorization proof, letting forged user operations consume more than 300 wallets' EntryPoint gas deposits.

sources.ref: verified Sodium implementation deployed by 0x0f369f61983cb0c4a432e4a81aaaa24f2d48be45 in tx 0x259d0c343896630f0a94cd7d4ff69fd489d424618368aa362a37b9662e21cce4; sampled victim wallets pointed to it before the attack

deployment-basis recheck: same implementation contract as the Lumi row. Its runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 142595379 and the incident block 483046805 and it holds no implementation slot of any kind; callTracer shows the exploit tx DELEGATECALLs *into* it from the wallet proxies (executeWithSodiumAuthSession / validateUserOp 0x3a871cdd), so the executing code is its own 2023 bytecode. The two delegatecall sites inside it are OpenZeppelin Address.functionDelegateCall and the caller-supplied Enum.Operation.DelegateCall path, neither an upgrade point. Deployment is exact; 995.0 days.

incident.name: Sonne Finance
incident.notes: Compound-v2 fork empty-market donation attack on the soVELO market, executed in the window between market creation (timelocked proposal execution) and collateral-factor guard.

sources.ref: onchain review (RPC only, Optimism): soVELO market 0xE3B81318B1b6776F0877c3770AfDdFf97b9f5fE5 (storage slot 1 name 'Sonne VelodromeV2', slot 2 symbol 'soVELO', slot 17 underlying 0x9560e827af36c94d2ac33a39bce1fe78631088db VELO) created 2024-05-10T13:40:13Z at block 119874818. Compound-v2 fork, but a non-delegating CErc20, not a CErc20Delegator: over [119874818, incident block 120044611] the market emits only the two constructor events of CToken.initialize (NewComptroller -> 0x60cf091cd3f50420d50fd7f707414d0df4751c58 and NewMarketInterestRateModel -> 0x7320bd5fa56f8a7ea959a425f0c0b8cac56f741e, both in the creation tx 0x307b85a2fe776aad28ecc347e73170706850fea560479c78e7705c9332fb0feb); there is no NewImplementation (0xd604de94d45953f9138079ec1b82d533cb2160c906d1076d1f7ed54befbca97a) and no EIP-1967 Upgraded (0xbc7cd75a20ee27fd9adebab32041f755214dbc6bffa90cc0225b39da2e5c2d3b) log at all. Cross-checked with storage: slot 18, which holds the implementation pointer on a delegator, is zero for the whole window. eth_getCode is byte-identical at the creation and incident blocks (14896 bytes) and the disassembled runtime contains zero DELEGATECALL opcodes (the only 0xf2/0xf5 bytes sit at offsets 14812-14839, past the last executable instruction, inside an embedded event-topic constant and the CBOR metadata trailer), so the code provably never changed. CONFIRMED: deployment basis is exact, codeAgeSeconds 339587 (3.9d) unchanged; the exploit window was opened by market configuration, not by a code change.

exploit tx backfilled and verified onchain (optimism block 120062493; victim in receipt logs): the first of two attack txs (DeFiHackLabs Attack Tx1); the second drain 0x9312ae377d7ebdf3c7c3a86f80514878deb5df51aad38b6191d55db53e42b7f0 followed 22 minutes later

incident.name: SpankChain LedgerChannel reentrancy
incident.notes: LedgerChannel opened a channel with an attacker-controlled ERC20 whose transfer() re-entered LCOpenTimeout()/consensusCloseChannel before the channel state was cleared, letting the attacker withdraw the channel's ETH repeatedly.

sources.ref: onchain review: LedgerChannel 0xf91546835f756DA0c10cFa0CDA95b15577b84aA7 created 2018-08-30T09:35:59Z by 0x406fffca2a6d1997b9ef573d67efe74ba786dff1, unrelated to the attack sender; no proxy, no upgrade events, age measured from deployment. Recheck (deployment basis confirmed): keccak(eth_getCode) is identical at the creation block 6239908 and the incident block 6467248; the six DELEGATECALLs in the runtime are calls into the ECTools library linked at deploy time (Etherscan's library map records ECTools:0xcb107c7d2a93e638b20342f46b10b9b6d81377bf, present as a PUSH20 constant in the bytecode), an address that cannot be repointed, and none of them is taken in the exploit trace.

incident.notes: The SPARTA/WBNB pool computed the burn payout in removeLiquidity() from its live token balances rather than its recorded baseAmount/tokenAmount reserves, so donating assets to the pool before burning LP units inflated the redemption above the LP's true share.

incident.name: SquidSwap unbounded internal swap sandwiched
incident.notes: SquidSwap's public swapTokens()/sellSwappedTokens() sell the contract's own SQUID holdings through PancakeSwap with no minimum-output check, so the attacker skewed the pool inside a PancakeV3 flash loan and sandwiched the contract's swap.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim 0xd309f0Fd5C3b90ecFb7024eDe7D329d9582492c5 created 2024-03-10T10:33:06Z by 0xff00d2d6210a537b517138389c29c8a6bb56dad7, which is not the attack-tx sender 0x418038cd60d7ad3006075411765c34048907e7e7; 0 EIP-1967 Upgraded events on the victim before the incident; code age measured from deployment (onchain).

incident.name: SSS
incident.notes: token self-transfer balance-inflation bug

incident.name: StackMarket flash-loan driven account-token round trip
incident.notes: StackMarket's account-token buy path could be driven with borrowed WETH and unwound through the matching Uniswap V3 pool inside one transaction, so a Morpho flash loan bought an account token and sold it straight back at a profit paid by the market.

sources.ref: onchain review: StackMarket 0x555555555a4161c1c0ba310fc1c993086d3de042 created 2024-12-07T05:35:53Z by 0x42c22ebd6f07fc052040137eeb3b8a1b7a38b275, not the attack-tx sender 0x97d8170e04771826a31c4c9b81e9f9191a1c8613; no EIP-1967 events, 91.0 days old. Classified economic-design: no code defect is identified, the pricing path simply admitted a profitable flash-loan round trip. 0.56 WETH x $2,150.20 at the incident timestamp (DefiLlama) = $1,204. Recheck (deployment basis confirmed): keccak(eth_getCode) on StackMarket is identical at the creation block 23380203 and the incident block 27309557, no EIP-1967 or beacon slot is set (slot 0 holds only the owner), and the single DELEGATECALL taken in the exploit goes to 0x83be7ba2891cd45002eff83d2836d5b9f2f6a1cf, which appears as a PUSH20 link-time library constant in the runtime and therefore cannot be repointed.

incident.name: StoneVault unprotected round settlement
incident.notes: StoneVault's round-advance entry point (selector 0x5069fb57) had no access control, so the attacker could deposit, settle the round themselves at a share price they had just moved, and withdraw at a profit in the same transaction.

sources.ref: onchain review: StoneVault 0xA62F9C5af106FeEE069F38dE51098D9d81B90572 (holding STONE 0x7122985656e38BDC0302Db86685bb972b145bD3C, StakeStone Ether) created 2023-09-24T06:20:23Z by 0xc1364ad857462e1b60609d9e56b5e24c5c21a312, unrelated to the attack sender; no EIP-1967 events, age from deployment (44.7 days). ~17 ETH x $1,886.72 at incidentTimestamp 1699400627 (DefiLlama) = $32,074. Recheck (deployment basis confirmed): keccak(eth_getCode) on StoneVault is identical at the creation block 18203833 and the incident block 18523441, no EIP-1967 or beacon slot is set, the exploit trace contains no DELEGATECALL out of the vault, and the single 0xf4 byte in the runtime lies inside trailing constant data rather than reachable code, so the vault's executing code is immutable.

incident.name: Starlink transfer business-logic flaw
incident.notes: The Starlink token's transfer logic moves tokens out of the liquidity pair's own balance without a sync(), so the attacker collapsed the reserve and swapped a small holding out for the pair's WBNB.

incident.name: Stars Arena share-buy reentrancy
incident.notes: The share-buy entry point (selector 0xe9ccf3a3) sent AVAX back to the caller before finalising share accounting, letting the attacker re-enter the weight-setting function (selector 0x5632b2e4) mid-call so that a single share could then be sold via sellShares() for ~266,000 AVAX.

incident.name: StrongBlock governance takeover
incident.notes: The attacker legitimately acquired majority voting weight in the abandoned Governor and used its proposal flow to seize the proxy upgrader before draining the service treasury.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim creator 0x4b5057b2c87ec9e7c047fb00c0e406dff2fdacad via 0xf1968991020f5551ccb9f76fdc8bd06dbd2b2638b88aced8909558d7b6f43344; not attacker

deployment-basis recheck: the victim is an AdminUpgradeabilityProxy, so the EIP-1967 implementation slot 0x360894a1...2bbc was read directly rather than trusted to events. It holds 0x145931a8add54e6e0c7753ee0a59ff9e7e2f488d at the creation block 11380285, at the block before the incident (25691526), at the incident block, and at all 41 evenly spaced samples in between, and the proxy's runtime bytecode is byte-identical at the creation and incident blocks; the later implementation 0xf6c7c78f8cec262eafc90f87a88fb5ef43f2e285 that Etherscan shows was installed only after the incident. callTracer on the attack tx also shows the drain executing through the Governor 0x53ca51ba980b6475c13d158c1825013cf81038fc and its logic 0xe89c0d3fce4eb31060b6a0329ba408029d0c4106, with no call reaching the victim proxy. incident.name: SubQuery Settings unprotected setBatchAddress
incident.notes: Settings.setBatchAddress()/setContractAddress() lacked the onlyOwner modifier, so the attacker repointed the StakingManager and RewardsDistributor registry entries at their own helper, which then passed Staking's address-based authorization checks and moved the Staking proxy's 218M SQT out via unbondCommission()/withdrawARequest().

sources.ref: onchain review: victim is the Settings TransparentUpgradeableProxy created 2024-02-13 by 0x70d0afee4a6a314d71046da9b4bbcfb8fd1722ce (not the attacker); its only pre-incident Upgraded event is the deployment-block one pointing at implementation 0xf282737992da4217bf5f8b6ae621181e84d7d3b9, the flawed Settings code named in the PoC. incident.name: SummerFi
incident.notes: FleetCommander NAV summed each Ark's totalAssets() with no manipulation guard, so donating cheap vgUSDC into an empty ark inflated share value and the attacker redeemed to drain other LPs.

incident.name: RareStakingV1 updateMerkleRoot access check
incident.notes: RareStakingV1.updateMerkleRoot() guarded itself with require(msg.sender != owner() || msg.sender != 0xc2F3...8ddc), a disjunction that is true for every caller, so the attacker installed their own claim root and drained the staking contract's RARE.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim is the ERC1967 staking proxy 0x3f4D74...8Eb48 (creator 0xdc005449848f65639d101a7d2b141c527e53f9d4, unrelated to the attacker); its implementation at the incident block was 0xffb512b9176d527c5d32189c3e310ed4ab2bb9ec (RareStakingV1) whose verified source contains the ||-instead-of-&& require in updateMerkleRoot; the proxy's RARE balance went from 11,907,874.71 to 0 across the attack tx

incident.name: SushiSwap RouteProcessor2 unvalidated route pool
incident.notes: RouteProcessor2.processRoute() never checked that the pool address encoded in the user-supplied `route` was a real UniswapV3 pool, so an attacker-controlled 'pool' could call back into uniswapV3SwapCallback and make the router execute transferFrom against any wallet that had approved it.

sources.ref: onchain review: RouteProcessor2 0x044b75f554b886a065b9567891e45c79542d7357 created 2023-04-05 by 0xf87bc5535602077d340806d71f805ea9907a843d (Sushi deployer), unrelated to the attack senders; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, so the exploited code was 3.8 days old. The flaw was exploited by many independent senders in blocks 17007838-17007844 draining approvals from 0x31d3243cfb54b34fc9c73e1cb1137124bd6b13e1; the tx recorded here is the 800 WETH drain named in Sushi's own post-mortem, sent by the MEV searcher c0ffeebabe.eth which returned funds, while other replays (e.g. 0x8ac0b9656b7c39be0d3d73828d2041e8c0e27712) kept them

incident.name: SVT pool flawed price calculation
incident.notes: The SVT pool derives the redemption price from its own token balance instead of a tracked accounting figure, so a direct SVT transfer into the pool inflated the redemption rate and let the attacker take out its USDT.

incident.name: SwapNet Router arbitrary call
incident.notes: The closed-source SwapNet Router's swap entrypoint (selector 0x87395540) performed a low-level call to a caller-supplied target with caller-supplied calldata and no target validation, so passing a token address made the router itself execute transferFrom() against users' standing infinite approvals.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim proxy created 2025-11-08 by 0x9cb8d9bae84830b7f5f11ee5048c04a80b8514ba (not the attacker); four Upgraded(address) events with the implementation in log data, the last on 2025-11-21 pointing at 0xdc3914ca7b18a2bf41b43a263258b71e32296d7d. incident.name: Swarm Markets xToken permissionless mint
incident.notes: The xToken contracts registered in Swarm's XTokenWrapper exposed mint(address,uint256) with no MINTER_ROLE check, so anyone could mint xDAI/xUSDC and redeem them through XTokenWrapper.unwrap() for the wrapper's real DAI and USDC.

sources.ref: onchain review: xToken 0xD08E245Fdb3f1504aea4056e2C71615DA7001440 created 2024-01-25T05:11:11Z by Swarm deployer 0x959e2cc532115d0a86e24eb2977d93df6202560e (also the creator of the second drained xToken 0x0a3fbF5B4cF80DB51fCAe21efe63f6a36D45d2B2), neither the attacker nor the attack-tx sender; its verified source has an unguarded `function mint(address account, uint256 amount) external { _mint(account, amount); }` and hasRole(MINTER_ROLE, attacker) is false, confirming no role was needed. No EIP-1967 events, code immutable since deployment. The cited transaction was submitted by MEV searcher 0xc0ffeebabe5d496b2dde509f9fa189c25cf29671, who front-ran the original exploiter 0x38f68f119243adbca187e1ef64344ed475a8c69c; ~7,729 in DAI+USDC drained from XTokenWrapper 0x2b9dc65253c035Eb21778cB3898eab5A0AdA0cCe.

incident.name: SynapLogic sale proxy unbounded referral rebates
incident.notes: The SYP sale proxy's buy path (selector 0x670a3267) paid a 10% rebate to every entry of a caller-supplied referrer array without bounding its length or checking that total payouts stayed under the payment received, so repeating the buyer's own address 31 times returned about 310% of each purchase in ETH and USDC.

sources.ref: onchain review: sale proxy created 2025-10-12 by 0xaf4d0fe93eeddabbd4ddb7451f09e6359575c214 (not the attacker); EIP-1967 impl slot held 0xc859ac8429fb4a5e24f24a7bed3fe3a8db4fb371 - the implementation named as vulnerable in the PoC - and the six Upgraded events on the proxy all land at Base blocks 41047082+, after the attack at block 41038634, so they are the emergency response, not a pre-incident change. Loss ~27.6 ETH + ~3,450 USDC; DefiLlama records $144,000 while smartcontractshacking.com lists $186,000. Recheck (deployment basis confirmed): rather than relying on the Upgraded events, the EIP-1967 implementation slot 0x3608...382bbc was binary-searched with eth_getStorageAt over [36732639, 41038633] and held 0xc859ac8429fb4a5e24f24a7bed3fe3a8db4fb371 unchanged for the whole pre-incident life of the proxy; that is also the only address the victim delegatecalls in the exploit trace (selector 0x670a3267). Confirms the six Upgraded events are post-incident and deployment is the right basis.

incident.name: tCDP transferFrom checks the wrong allowance
incident.notes: tCDP.transferFrom() debits _allowed[msg.sender][to] instead of checking _allowed[from][msg.sender], so a self-approval let the attacker move every outstanding tCDP balance out of three unrelated holders and burn it to redeem the contract's Compound ETH collateral.

incident.notes: TcrToken exposed a mint/exchange path that let the attacker obtain TCR without paying for it and redeem it against the project's USDT pool 0x420725a69e79eeffb000f98ccd78a52369b6c5d4, emptying the pool in one transaction.

incident.name: Telcoin CloneableProxy re-initialisation
incident.notes: The Telcoin wallet CloneableProxy left its OpenZeppelin _initialized flag clear, so anyone could call initialize(address,bytes) again to point the proxy at their own implementation and have it delegatecall arbitrary code that transferred out the wallet's TEL.

sources.ref: onchain review: CloneableProxy 0x56BCADff30680EBB540a84D75c182A5dC61981C0 created 2021-11-23T10:50:52Z by 0x0d0fbdfb774049aea1aaf8d88cd41cd10830c5a3, not the attack-tx sender 0xdb4b84f0e601e40a02b54497f26e03ef33f3a5b7; no EIP-1967 Upgraded event, 762.3 days old. The PoC reads storage slot 0 before and after and shows _initialized flipping from 0 to 1 during the exploit, confirming the proxy had never been marked initialised. Reported loss ~$1.24M across the wallet clones drained in the campaign.

deployment-basis recheck: the CloneableProxy's 45-byte runtime is an EIP-1167 clone of the fixed master 0x10d0e9755c67ab37089acb4f51e8b4ee407fe853, and the master in turn delegatecalls the address in the EIP-1967 beacon slot. prestateTracer on the attack tx shows that slot held 0x3f443c31dab3dab882f9fe621f97b74c3c14837d before the exploit, and the exploit's re-initialisation is precisely what overwrote it with the attacker module 0x10e5c8d3537856f141272e1c39befdab4dd8bde0 that is then delegatecalled. Binary-searching the slot over [21704647, 51546495] (i.e. up to the block before the incident) shows 0x3f443c31... constant from creation; the runtimes of both the master and 0x3f443c31... are byte-identical at the creation and incident blocks. Deployment is the correct basis; 762.3 days.

incident.name: Themis
incident.notes: Themis lending oracle prices a Balancer wstETH-WETH LP the attacker manipulated to over-borrow reserves.

sources.ref: Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the victim is an ERC1967 proxy; its implementation slot holds 0x848f29fe9e3f0ba67095c26ebe48648ccfd8148d at both the creation block 101340897 and the incident block 105524524, with a binary search of eth_getStorageAt over that range finding no intermediate write, and the proxy runtime is byte-identical at both blocks. incident.name: Thena reward pool unprotected unstake
incident.notes: The Thena reward pool's unstake(address,uint256,address,bool) accepts an arbitrary token and pool from any caller and transfers the balance out without checking the caller's stake, so a freshly deployed contract could call it and take the pool's BUSD.

deployment-basis recheck: the victim is an Aragon AppProxyUpgradeable, whose executing code comes from the Kernel rather than from any slot on the proxy itself. Its AppStorage slots resolve as documented - kernel at keccak('aragonOS.appStorage.kernel') = 0x4172f0f7...137b holds 0xbf478b6f3adf3b9683e8591d9295f86039e7ac46, appId at keccak('aragonOS.appStorage.appId') = 0xd6254962...639b holds 0x9fa3927f639745e587912d4b0fea7ef9013bf93fb907d29faeab57417ba6e1d4 - and callTracer confirms the proxy DELEGATECALLs 0xb935c3d80229d5d92f3761b17cd81dc2610e3a45. Binary-searching the Kernel's apps[keccak('base')][appId] entry (slot keccak(appId . keccak(keccak('base') . 0)) = 0xbf596794...c178) over [12003000, 25279892] shows a single write, at block 12003441 / 2021-03-09T09:14:54Z - the victim's own deployment block and timestamp - and no change since. The second DELEGATECALL in the tx, to the CallsScript EVM script executor 0x5ceb19e1890f677c3676d5ecdf7c501eba01a054, is to a 2019 contract whose runtime is byte-identical at both blocks. Deployment is the correct basis; 1918.1 days.

incident.name: Tornado Cash governance takeover via mutated proposal
incident.notes: Not a defect in Tornado's deployed code: proposal 20 passed the DAO's normal vote-and-execute path with legitimately delegated TORN, and Governance.execute() delegatecalled the proposal exactly as designed - the attacker had merely self-destructed and CREATE2-redeployed the proposal contract with hidden code after voting closed, minting 1.2M votes to sybil addresses and then draining ~483k TORN from the governance vault.

sources.ref: onchain review (no exploit tx in this row; DeFiHackLabs src/test/2022-10/TransitSwap_exp.sol documents the attack. Incident block located by binary-searching eth_getBlockByNumber to measurement.incidentTimestamp -> bsc block 21808649, 2022-10-01T12:00:00Z). The exchange is a 46-byte Vyper forwarder whose runtime hardcodes the Uniswap V1 exchange template 0x2157a7894439191e520825fe9399ab8655e0f708 as a PUSH20 immediate, so the delegate target cannot be repointed; the template's runtime is byte-identical at 13 sample points across [9059910, 9894154] and callTracer on the exploit tx confirms the forwarder delegatecalls only the template.

sources.ref: onchain review (Ethereum). Victim: StabilizerNFT ERC1967Proxy 0x1346b4d6867a382b02b19a8d131d9b96b18585f2, created 2025-09-16T13:01:59Z block 23375794 by the USPD deployer 0x555350445E1f1ca212edB8cF397a383695ff7a36 in tx 0x3477bb4cb7cfcd12664ca224ad8468cfe2168fa1e779333c847a02bea1623d23 — not the attacker and not the exploit-tx sender 0x083379bdac3e138cb0c7210e0282fbc466a3215a, so rule 2 holds. Note that public write-ups label 0x11a880b0c9d50b4aef7527d458497e60fa602429 the 'proxy contract'; onchain that address is the audited StabilizerNFT *implementation* (24 KB of runtime code, same deployer), so the row uses the proxy. Timeline from the proxy's Upgraded logs plus eth_getStorageAt on slot 0x360894a13ba1a3210667c828492db98dca3e2076cc3735a920a3ca505d382bbc: 2025-09-16T13:01:59Z block 23375794 creation -> 0x11a880b0... ; 2025-09-16T13:02:11Z block 23375795 tx 0xc0b7e490caac2b8cfa5e62d1b28a5e7dba7600e623c71352acbc9b23c2b65b7c, sent by 0x7C97313f349608f59A07C23b18Ce523A33219d83 through Multicall3, front-runs the team's initialize(): it emits Initialized(1) and RoleGranted for DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and role 0x189ab7a9244df0848122154315af71fe140f3db0fe014031783b0946b8c9d2e3 to 0xc2a0ad4bd62676692f9dca88b750bec98e526c42, then Upgraded -> 0xac075b9bf166e5154cc98f62ee7b94e5345cc090 (clandestine implementation, itself deployed 2025-07-28 by unrelated CPIMP infrastructure 0xac82fa44b7e2c71db3931a47698de656ed6d2fca) followed by a second Upgraded in the same tx claiming 0x11a880b0... again — the slot really reads 0xac075b9b... at the end of that block, so the second event is spoofed; 2025-09-17T18:57:47Z block 23384737 the slot is silently restored to the audited 0x11a880b0... with no Upgraded event at all; 2025-12-04T12:35:23Z block 23939725 tx 0xe6715708c0e3b2b3a0a10ab1b25785b8d04db09ef71196c5ea313d8a0676f823 upgrades to 0x4c4eacbe5d5232698d12c379be14a0e561001c21, deployed 12 seconds earlier by the attacker; 2025-12-04T18:08:23Z the drain tx itself upgrades to 0xa3d2616ee942b36648eaa55976ee7b761bd2a21b (deployed by the attack sender ~6 minutes before). Age is measured from 2025-09-17T18:57:47Z, the last change to the victim's executing code that is not part of the attack's own execution: from that moment the audited implementation ran continuously for ~78 days. The two December implementation writes are the exploit machinery (contracts deployed by the attacker seconds before use) and are excluded; taking the December upgrade instead would give 19,980 s and measuring from deployment 6,843,984 s. verify.mjs, which takes the max Upgraded timestamp, would derive 0 s because the last Upgraded event is emitted inside the drain tx — hence the documented-change basis. Loss from the drain tx logs: 232.9651 + 3.7293 + 0.1485 = 236.8429 stETH to the attacker at stETH/USD 3153.719722543291 (curl https://coins.llama.fi/prices/historical/1764871703/coingecko:staked-ether; coingecko:ethereum reads 3153.449311643833 at the same timestamp) = $746,936, plus 302,908.86 USDC pulled out of the USPD/USDC pool 0x06cf5f9b93e9fcfdb33d6b3791eb152567cd8d36 = $1,049,845 total. The 3,121.95 WETH is a Balancer flash loan, repaid in the same tx; the 10 mint cycles issue 9,845,436.95 USPD each (98,454,369 USPD total) and the residual 1,621,355 USPD/USDC LP tokens the attacker keeps are backed by that unbacked USPD and are not counted.

incident.notes: UwU Lend's Aave-fork LendingPool priced sUSDE from an oracle reading Curve pool spot state, so a flash-loan sequence that skewed those pools inflated sUSDE collateral value and let the attacker borrow out most of the protocol's other markets.

sources.ref: onchain review: LendingPool proxy 0x2409aF0251DCB89EE3Dee572629291f9B087c668 (verified as InitializableImmutableAdminUpgradeabilityProxy) created 2022-09-19T16:55:47Z by 0x50831130c4b0aa78fca9edaa39d7339a9620d751, not the attack-tx sender 0x841ddf093f5188989fa1524e7b893de64b421f47. It emits no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, so the EIP-1967 implementation slot was read directly: 0x05bfa9157e92690b179033ca2f6dd1e86b25ea4d at the creation block, the pre-incident block 20061318 and today alike, confirming the implementation never changed and age runs from deployment (629.8 days). A second exploit on the same pool three days later (tx 0x9235e0662e230bdfa94f56f4932fd09a95fea17e4b9b44a4f40a59449e216110, ~$3.7M, src/test/2024-06/UwuLend_Second_exp.sol) is the same victim contract and root cause and is not recorded as a separate row.

deployment-basis recheck extended to the whole delegate set: callTracer shows the LendingPool proxy delegatecalling 0x05bfa9157e92690b179033ca2f6dd1e86b25ea4d (the EIP-1967 implementation) plus the Aave-style linked libraries 0x3c0ada81038a078cc1272ac22745ddd1ab8839af and 0xaede01960810a655aecf86278bfdf5c968198b89, which are link-time constants inside that implementation and cannot be repointed. The implementation slot returns 0x05bfa915... at the creation block 15568883, at the incident block 20061319 and at all 201 evenly spaced samples in between, and the proxy runtime is byte-identical at both blocks. Deployment is the correct basis; 629.8 days.

incident.name: Value DeFi vSafe WBNB vault cross-contract reentrancy
incident.lossOther: ~$11M reported across the affected Value DeFi pools and the vSafe multi-strategy WBNB vault
incident.notes: The vSafe WBNB vault's deposit/share calculation read its Alpaca ibBNB position mid-flight, so reentering deposit() from inside Alpaca Vault.work() minted the attacker vault shares against balances that had not yet been settled.

sources.ref: onchain review: vault 0xD4BBF439d3EAb5155Ca7c0537E583088fB4CFCe8 created 2021-03-05 by the Value DeFi deployer 0x9696969e67b37403196a3519edc176276714a724, unrelated to attack sender 0xcb36b1ee0af68dce5578a487ff2da81282512233; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events between creation and the incident block 7223030, so age measured from deployment. No high-confidence per-contract USD figure exists, so lossUsd is null; the incident is reported at ~$11M, far above the $1,000 floor.

incident.name: Vault4626 idle-WETH totalAssets inflation
incident.notes: totalAssets() quotes idle non-asset WETH sitting in the vault into USDC asset terms while redeem() pays the redeemer both the USDC asset value and the underlying WETH itself, so the attacker deposited flash-loaned USDC for nearly all the shares, donated WETH to inflate totalAssets, and redeemed to take the donated WETH back plus the vault's share of it - a double-count in the vault's own accounting.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim recorded as the live vault proxy 0x72dbAA8A09d71D09c6De0de439968e1E7c122020 rather than the implementation 0xD08579102fc28355C5839019b730Ce58F84E6a4d that DeFiHackLabs labels 'vulnerable contract' - the implementation holds no state and no funds, while the proxy is the ERC-4626 vault the attacker deposited into and redeemed from, and only the proxy carries the code-change history the age is measured over. Both were created by 0xc7d5acaea25f06450aae5a6ee0ec5f70d4fe355f, unrelated to attack sender 0xA27eAE743Cd8C03E9b7c25ebF43DADbBC6Df9bFA (whose attack contract 0x870e3d0f18ce5e0894e206c68885f2b6dba16199 was created by the exploit transaction itself). The proxy was created 2026-05-02 at block 45671620 and emits standard EIP-1967 Upgraded events: 8 of them up to the incident (blocks 45671620, 45671736, 46166499, 46284783, 46459149, 46459157, 47019073, 47190063), the last installing exactly the flawed implementation 0xd08579102fc28355c5839019b730ce58f84e6a4d at 2026-06-11T09:17:53Z, 17.79 days before the exploit. Loss not recorded in USD: the attacker's WETH balance rose from 4.837426 to 18.366634 WETH across the transaction, i.e. 13.529208 WETH, matching the ~13.53 WETH in the DeFiHackLabs PoC. Order-of-magnitude sanity check only: 13.5 ETH is far above the $1,000 floor at any plausible ETH price.
loss converted at the incident timestamp (1782706497) via DefiLlama coins: 13.53 WETH x $1,577.71 = $21,346

incident.name: VDS
incident.notes: sending VDS to its own contract redeems AVD 1:1, mismatched from the deposit ratio, letting the attacker extract AVD.

sources.ref: Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the victim sets no EIP-1967 implementation or beacon slot and its runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 52614868 and the incident block 54252254; all eight DELEGATECALL sites are solc external-library calls to the PUSH20 constant 0x1f428ffb964de7d906278382ba8902e3290f83a1 (preceded by the usual EXTCODESIZE guard), a library deployed 23 blocks before the victim by the same creator 0x6c8abda36388b15c011d9ee93a811d36df8baaaa and byte-identical over the window, so the target cannot be repointed.

incident.name: Velocore ConstantProductPool fee underflow
incident.notes: Velocore's ConstantProductPool computed its swap fee with an unchecked multiplier that overflows once a single withdrawal takes effectively the whole LP supply, so a flash-loaned burn of the USDC/ETH VLP returned far more than the pool held and drained it through the vault's execute path.

sources.ref: onchain review over a Linea archive RPC (linea-rpc.publicnode.com; the l2beat Linea endpoint does not serve 2024 blocks): the USDC/ETH VLP pool 0xe2c67A9B15e9E7FF8A9Cb0dFb8feE5609923E5DB was created at block 128549, 2023-08-05T05:24:29Z, by the Velocore factory deployer 0xca0671f5c50e4f28ae847480ee24cfe11c5c1b35, not the attack-tx sender 0x8cdc37ed79c5ef116b9dc2a53cb86acaca3716bf; cast logs finds no Upgraded event on the pool before the incident block 5079177 (2024-06-02T02:37:29Z), so the executing code was 301.7 days old. Swaps are routed through the Velocore vault 0x1d0188c4B276A09366D05d6Be06aF61a73bC7535. Loss ~$6.88M as previously recorded.

incident.name: Venus zkSync wUSDM market donation attack
incident.notes: The newly listed vUSDM market had a near-empty supply, so donating wUSDM directly to it inflated the exchange rate enough that a rounding-truncated position could be liquidated and the vWETH market's collateral seized.

sources.ref: onchain review over the zkSync Era RPC (Etherscan has no creation API for this chain): binary search over eth_getCode places vUSDM 0x183dE3C349fCf546aAe925E1c7F364EA6FB4033c first having code at block 53902189, 2025-01-17T14:42:49Z, and the attack-tx sender is 0x16be708e257a0df0f4275ecd9b0f70ce4b45430c. It is a BeaconProxy: the EIP-1967 implementation slot is empty and the beacon slot holds 0x53523537aa330640b80400eb8b309ff5896e7eb5; cast logs finds no Upgraded event on that beacon between block 53000000 and the incident block 56669987, so the executing code has been unchanged since the proxy was created, 40.5 days before the incident. 86.72 WETH x $2,334.28 at the incident timestamp (DefiLlama) = $202,428. Recheck (deployment basis confirmed, storage rather than events): at the incident block the vUSDM proxy's EIP-1967 beacon slot held 0x53523537aa330640b80400eb8b309ff5896e7eb5 and that beacon's implementation (its storage slot 1) held 0x6829ff2937f780ed01a4ce3fda3d0ba63b1bd771; binary-searching eth_getStorageAt on both slots over [53902189, 56669986] found no change, and keccak(eth_getCode) on the proxy is identical at the two blocks, so the executing code is unchanged since the proxy was created.

incident.name: VerusBridge
incident.notes: Verus submitImports accepted a crafted partialtransactionproof/MMR proof that bypassed VerusProof validation, minting fake ETH/tBTC/USDC imports.

incident.notes: The bridge accepted notarization bytes whose duplicate state-root entries were interpreted differently by Verus and Ethereum, installing an attacker-chosen root and authorizing unbacked imports.

incident.name: vETH
incident.notes: Vulnerable factory function (selector 0x6c0472da) lets attacker extract vETH/BIF value, working as designed but with a logic flaw draining the pair.

incident.name: VINU public addLiquidityETH with caller-supplied router
incident.notes: VINU.addLiquidityETH(router, to, pair) was public and took the router address from the caller, so the attacker passed a fake router, moved the token side of the pair at will, synced the reserves and swapped the whole ETH reserve out.

sources.ref: onchain review: VINU 0xF7ef0D57277ad6C2baBf87aB64bA61AbDd2590D2 created 2023-06-06T10:46:47Z by 0x42b9b986e14be1483ecf5f2af7f713f2c6558d75 - 19.8 minutes before the incident - and that deployer is not the attack sender 0x9748c854... nor its funder; the deployer's own tx list shows it deploying VINU and adding liquidity, i.e. a genuine (very fresh) launch that was exploited immediately. No EIP-1967 events, age from deployment (1,188 seconds). Loss ~$6K per the PoC header, taken in ETH.

incident.name: Visor Finance RewardsHypervisor unvalidated depositor
incident.notes: RewardsHypervisor.deposit() took the caller-supplied `from` contract at face value, reading IVisor(from).owner() as authorization and calling IVisor(from).delegatedTransferERC20() for payment, so an attacker contract that returned itself as owner and no-opped the transfer minted vVISR shares without depositing any VISR.

incident.name: VISTA flash-loan burn ignores frozen balances
incident.notes: VISTA's flash-loan path burns the borrowed tokens on repayment without checking whether the balance it burns is frozen, letting the attacker convert frozen presale allocations into free supply and sell it.

incident.name: VTF reward calculation flaw
incident.notes: VTF's reward accounting credits a holder's share from their instantaneous balance rather than an accrued stake, so the attacker cycled a large borrowed balance through the reward claim and drained the contract's USDT.

incident.name: VTSwapHook pre-fee reserve update
incident.notes: VTSwapHook priced its nonlinear VT/T curve on fee-adjusted amounts but wrote back reserves using the full pre-fee specified amount, so alternating an exact-input ATH->vATH swap with an exact-output vATH->ATH swap left the caller with positive Uniswap V4 PoolManager deltas in both currencies.

sources.ref: onchain review: VTSwapHook 0xbf4b4A83708474528A93C123F817e7f2A0637a88 created 2025-07-25T09:06:29Z by 0x1e1840f1eb9d9b89f4b1f2ad469e31e9877b820d, not the attack-tx sender 0xf378840de079c70f55218cd3af99d2d81ba154ba; no EIP-1967 events, 245.7 days old. Loss stated only in vATH and ATH, whose price is bound to the exploited pool, so no USD figure is asserted; at the widely quoted ATH price of a few cents the 2.0M ATH leg alone is far above the $1,000 floor.

incident.name: Warp Finance LP collateral valuation manipulation
incident.notes: WarpControl valued deposited Uniswap V2 LP collateral from the pair's live spot reserves, so a flash-loaned swap that doubled the WETH-DAI LP price let the attacker borrow 3.86m DAI and 3.9m USDC against collateral worth a fraction of that; the lending code itself behaved as written.

Created 2020-12-16 by 0x8f3e8a974d6eb27316054147fdf0e960dab2e1b3, not by attack sender 0xebc6bd6a - only 1.7 days before the incident, matching Warp's 2020-12-09 launch. lossUsd is the borrowed 3.86m DAI + 3.9m USDC, both USD-pegged 1:1

incident.name: VerifierExit exit-proof verification always returning true
incident.notes: ZKSwap 1.0's VerifierExit began verifyExitProof() with an unconditional `return true`, so once the rollup was pushed into Exodus Mode the attacker's forged exit proofs against the frozen state root were accepted and the L1 bridge released its balances.

sources.ref: callTracer review of the fake-exit tx: the attacker contract 0x2D3103c8Fdd9d9411E24f555fdad6B22F29F613A calls the ZKSwap bridge proxy 0x8ECa806Aecc86CE90Da803b080Ca4E3A9b8097ad (selector 0xd6973fc6) which STATICCALLs the VerifierExit proxy 0x961369d3...f521f 15 times with selector 0xc81a27ad, every one returning 0x...01 for a forged proof; bridge storage slot 6 holds the VerifierExit address, both proxies were created in the same 2021-02-12 deployment tx by 0x7d1a14eed7af8e26f24bf08ba6ed7a339abcf037 (not the attacker), and the VerifierExit proxy has emitted no logs at all in its lifetime, so it was never upgraded; the exodus trigger was tx 0xfdb93e00f3b1d24303db7f43eaa5ef50d3fde957ddeec7c0feb8c5497ba11182

deployment-basis recheck (storage, not events): the VerifierExit proxy's single DELEGATECALL in the exploit tx (selector 0xc81a27ad) goes to 0xd12f4d8329584f36aed67f807f42d9a02beb9534, and the EIP-1967 implementation slot holds that address at the creation block 11841962, at the incident block 22882195 and at all 41 evenly spaced samples in between; the proxy runtime is byte-identical at both blocks. The always-true verifier really was the 2021 deployment; 1607.6 days.

Repeated through five CREATE2 helper contracts, each capped at 30,265,400 ZOOMER. Loss converted at the incident timestamp: 17.15 ETH x $2,927.14 (DefiLlama historical ETH price) = $50,200.

incident.name: USD0PPSubVault deployer-key compromise and malicious upgrade
incident.notes: No contract flaw: Zoth's deployer key held the UUPS upgrade authority for the USD0PPSubVaultUpgradeable proxy, and whoever obtained it called upgradeToAndCall() to install a self-authored implementation with an unrestricted withdraw(), emptying the vault 36 seconds later.

sources.ref: onchain review: proxy 0x82f3a039...e43e was created by Zoth deployer 0x3604582f56565d7060D73829FfB9EBD579218Dca (not the attack sender 0x3b33c5Cd...); the last of its seven Upgraded events, at block 22094140 in tx 0xb2335f7bf58abbcaa006d0a2bed7db2c64a5dabed56fb1759260adc012c49abe, installed the attacker's own implementation 0xc89d7894341e13d5067d003af5346b257d861f56 — so the mechanical code age of 36s measures the attacker's implementation, not Zoth's; this row is context only and never feeds the curve

incident.name: ZS destory_pair_amount pair drain
incident.notes: ZS exposes a permissionless destory_pair_amount() that deletes the ZS/BUSDT pair's ZS balance; the attacker called it and then sync()ed the pair to sell into the inflated price.
